model.mpi_analytics.mart__item_price_com.description:
Mart of invoice line-items built from `int__invoice_items_with_rerated_pricing`.
Produces one row per invoice line (filtered to non-empty item and non-null cost) and computes ranking metrics to identify the lowest cost (and most recent) rows per supplier and per item mapping.
`item_cost` and `item_quantity` reflect Y & S BOX→EACH rerating (issue #899) so the cheapest-by-cost rankings aren't skewed by UOM mismatches.
Source: `int__invoice_items_with_rerated_pricing`
(filtered: `item IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(item) <> '' AND cost IS NOT NULL AND matched_supplier_id IS NOT NULL`).

invoice_items_id.name: invoice_items_id
invoice_items_id.description: Primary key from source `int__invoice_items_with_rerated_pricing.invoice_items_id`. Represents the original invoice item identifier. Row is included only when this id exists in the source. Used to trace back to the raw invoice item row.

filename.name: filename
filename.description: Filename from `int__invoice_items_with_rerated_pricing.filename`. Useful for tracing back to the original invoice file.

item_code.name: item_code
item_code.description: Raw item code from `int__invoice_items_with_rerated_pricing.item`. Rows are filtered to exclude NULL or empty values (`TRIM(item) <> ''`).

item_cost.name: item_cost
item_cost.description: Item cost from `int__invoice_items_with_rerated_pricing.rerated_cost` (Y & S BOX→EACH-corrected per-unit cost).           Used for price comparison and ordering when computing rank fields.

is_price_rerated.name: is_price_rerated
is_price_rerated.description: TRUE when `item_cost` and `item_quantity` were corrected by the Y & S UOM rerating rule.

original_current_price.name: original_current_price
original_current_price.description: Raw per-unit cost before rerating. Equals `item_cost` when not rerated.

original_current_qty.name: original_current_qty
original_current_qty.description: Raw quantity before rerating. Equals `item_quantity` when not rerated.

purchase_date.name: purchase_date
purchase_date.description: Invoice date from `int__invoice_items_with_rerated_pricing.date`. Used as a tie-breaker (most recent) when ordering ranks.

supplier_id.name: supplier_id
supplier_id.description: Matched supplier identifier from `int__invoice_items_with_rerated_pricing.matched_supplier_id`. Rows are filtered to exclude NULL supplier ids.

rank_by_item_code.name: rank_by_item_code
rank_by_item_code.description: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY item, matched_supplier ORDER BY cost ASC, date DESC). Rank of the row for the raw item code per supplier; lower = cheaper (prefers most recent on ties).

rank_by_item_mpi_code.name: rank_by_item_mpi_code
rank_by_item_mpi_code.description: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY resolved_mpi_item, matched_supplier ORDER BY cost ASC, date DESC). Rank of the row for the resolved MPI item per supplier; lower = cheaper (prefers most recent on ties).

rank_by_item_and_item_mpi_code.name: rank_by_item_and_item_mpi_code
rank_by_item_and_item_mpi_code.description: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY item, resolved_mpi_item, matched_supplier ORDER BY cost ASC, date DESC). Rank when grouping by both raw item and MPI item within each supplier; useful to identify best price for a given combination of raw and resolved item mappings.

cheapest_rank_by_item_and_mpi_code.name: cheapest_rank_by_item_and_mpi_code
cheapest_rank_by_item_and_mpi_code.description: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY item, resolved_mpi_item, matched_supplier ORDER BY cost ASC, date DESC). Rank of the row for the raw item and MPI item per supplier; lower = cheaper (prefers most recent on ties).

latest_rank_by_item_code.name: latest_rank_by_item_code
latest_rank_by_item_code.description: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY item, matched_supplier ORDER BY date DESC, cost ASC). Rank of the row for the raw item per supplier; latest = recent (prefers lower cost on ties).

latest_rank_by_mpi_item_code.name: latest_rank_by_mpi_item_code
latest_rank_by_mpi_item_code.description: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY resolved_mpi_item, matched_supplier ORDER BY date DESC, cost ASC). Rank of the row for the MPI item per supplier; latest = recent (prefers lower cost on ties)

latest_rank_by_item_and_mpi_code.name: latest_rank_by_item_and_mpi_code

WITH prioritized_line_items AS (

        invoice_items_id,

            PARTITION BY item, matched_supplier
            ORDER BY rerated_cost ASC, date DESC
        ) AS rank_by_item_code,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY resolved_mpi_item, matched_supplier
            ORDER BY rerated_cost ASC, date DESC
        ) AS rank_by_item_mpi_code,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY item, resolved_mpi_item, matched_supplier
            ORDER BY rerated_cost ASC, date DESC

        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY item, matched_supplier

        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY resolved_mpi_item, matched_supplier
            ORDER BY date DESC, rerated_cost ASC
        ) AS latest_rank_by_mpi_item_code,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY item, resolved_mpi_item, matched_supplier

    FROM {{ ref('int__invoice_items_with_rerated_pricing') }}
    WHERE item IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(item) <> ''
        AND cost IS NOT NULL
        AND matched_supplier_id IS NOT NULL
        AND invoice_voided_at IS NULL
)

    *
FROM prioritized_line_items

model.mpi_analytics.int__invoice_items_w.name: int__invoice_items_with_rerated_pricing
model.mpi_analytics.int__invoice_items_w.description:
Adds Y & S "BOX vs EACH" UOM mismatch price **rerating** on top of
`int__invoice_items_with_normalized_fields`.

**Why this layer exists:**
The Price Changes mart (`mart__price_increases`) detects suspected UOM
mismatches for `Y & S Plumbing Supply` and recomputes the per-unit price.
That correction must propagate to every other surface the App shows
(Data Review, QuickBooks, Mapping, Purchase Order, Supplier Comparison).
Rather than duplicate the logic in every downstream mart, the rerating is
applied once in this intermediate layer and the corrected values
(`rerated_cost`, `rerated_qty`) are exposed to all consumers.

**Detection rule** (kept in lock-step with `mart__price_increases`):
  - `vendor = 'Y & S Plumbing Supply'`
  - has a previous purchase of the same item from the same vendor
  - `((cost - previous_cost) / previous_cost) * 100 > price_increase_threshold`

**Correction rule:**
  - `ratio        = ROUND(cost / previous_cost)`
  - `rerated_cost = ROUND(cost / NULLIF(ratio, 0), 2)`
  - `rerated_qty  = qty * NULLIF(ratio, 0)`

Total spend (`cost * qty`) is preserved by construction so reconciliation
against bill amounts is unaffected.

**Column strategy (additive):**
The raw `cost` and `qty` columns from upstream are passed through
unchanged. Rerated values are exposed in new columns so downstream marts
can pick whichever is appropriate for their use case.

**Threshold configuration:**
Driven by the `price_increase_threshold` dbt var, sourced from
`DBT_PRICE_INCREASE_THRESHOLD` env var (default 250).

**Downstream consumers:**
  - `mart__invoice_items`           (Data Review)
  - `mart__invoice_items_map`       (Mapping / QuickBooks export)
  - `mart__item_price_comparison`   (Purchase Order / Supplier Comparison)
  - `mart__mapping_audit`
  - `mart__address_sheet_aggregates`

`mart__price_increases` intentionally still computes its own rerating from
`int__invoice_items_with_normalized_fields` and is **not** migrated here
yet — see issue #899.

invoice_items_id.name: invoice_items_id
invoice_items_id.description: Primary key. Inherited from upstream; one row per invoice line.

cost.name: cost
cost.description:
Raw per-unit cost from upstream, **unchanged**. Use `rerated_cost`
when displaying values that may be affected by Y & S UOM rerating.

qty.name: qty
qty.description:
Raw quantity from upstream, **unchanged**. Use `rerated_qty` when
displaying values that may be affected by Y & S UOM rerating.

rerated_cost.name: rerated_cost
rerated_cost.description:
Per-unit cost after Y & S BOX→EACH correction.
Equals `cost` when `is_price_rerated = FALSE`.
May be negative for credit memos (passed through unchanged).

rerated_qty.name: rerated_qty
rerated_qty.description:
Quantity after Y & S BOX→EACH correction (multiplied by the rounded
BOX→EACH ratio so total spend is preserved).
Equals `qty` when `is_price_rerated = FALSE`.

is_price_rerated.name: is_price_rerated
is_price_rerated.description:
TRUE when this row's `cost`/`qty` were corrected by the Y & S UOM
mismatch rule. Used by the FE to surface a tooltip explaining the
adjustment.

original_current_price.name: original_current_price
original_current_price.description:
Snapshot of the raw `cost` at the time of rerating. Mirrors the
column name used by `mart__price_increases` (PR #906).
Always equals `cost`.

original_current_qty.name: original_current_qty
original_current_qty.description:
Snapshot of the raw `qty` at the time of rerating. Mirrors the
column name used by `mart__price_increases` (PR #906).
Always equals `qty`.

previous_cost.name: previous_cost
previous_cost.description:
Per-unit `cost` from the immediately preceding non-voided purchase of
the same item from the same vendor. NULL for the first purchase or
when current row has invalid cost / is voided.

previous_qty.name: previous_qty
previous_qty.description:
`qty` from the immediately preceding non-voided purchase of the same
item from the same vendor. NULL for the first purchase or when
current row has invalid cost / is voided.

previous_date.name: previous_date
previous_date.description:
`date` of the immediately preceding non-voided purchase of the same
item from the same vendor. NULL for the first purchase or when
current row has invalid cost / is voided.

model.mpi_analytics.int__invoice_items_w.raw_code:
/*
Invoice Items with Rerated Pricing

Adds Y & S (BOX vs EACH UOM mismatch) price rerating on top of the normalized
intermediate. Downstream marts that need rerated cost/qty (Data Review, Price
Changes, QuickBooks, Mapping, Purchase Order, Supplier Comparison) should source
from this model instead of `int__invoice_items_with_normalized_fields`.

What this model adds vs upstream:
  - previous_cost, previous_qty, previous_date  (LAG by item+vendor, date ASC)
  - is_price_rerated                            (TRUE when threshold tripped for Y&S)
  - rerated_cost, rerated_qty                   (corrected EACH-equivalent values)
  - original_current_price, original_current_qty (= cost / qty, kept for clarity)

The detection and correction rules are kept in lock-step with the equivalent
CTEs in `mart__price_increases.sql`. Voided rows and rows with non-positive
cost are excluded from the LAG window (matching `mart__price_increases`) so
they neither receive a `previous_cost` nor anchor one for later rows.

Detection rule:
  vendor = 'Y & S Plumbing Supply'
  AND previous_cost IS NOT NULL AND previous_cost > 0
  AND ((cost - previous_cost) / previous_cost * 100) > price_increase_threshold

Correction rule (preserves total spend cost*qty):
  ratio          = ROUND(cost / previous_cost)
  rerated_cost   = ROUND((cost / NULLIF(ratio, 0))::numeric, 2)
  rerated_qty    = qty  * NULLIF(ratio, 0)

The raw `cost` and `qty` columns are preserved unchanged so consumers can choose
which value to expose. Columns are additive.

Materialization:
  Full-refresh table. The LAG window requires the complete history per
  (item, vendor) pair, so we rebuild from scratch each run (mirrors the strategy
  used by `mart__price_increases`). Cost is amortized across all downstream marts.

Lineage:
  int__invoice_items_mapped
    → int__invoice_items_with_normalized_fields
      → THIS MODEL
        → mart__invoice_items, mart__invoice_items_map,
          mart__item_price_comparison, mart__mapping_audit,
          mart__address_sheet_aggregates
*/

{% set price_increase_threshold = var('price_increase_threshold') %}

{{ config(
    materialized='table',
    schema='intermediate',
    tags=['intermediate', 'pricing', 'rerating'],
    indexes=[
        {'columns': ['invoice_items_id'], 'unique': True},
        {'columns': ['item', 'vendor']},
        {'columns': ['is_active']},
        {'columns': ['_dbt_updated_at']},
        {'columns': ['is_overridden']},
        {'columns': ['invoice_voided_at']},
        {'columns': ['is_price_rerated']}
    ],
    post_hook=[
        "ANALYZE {{ this }}"
    ]
) }}

WITH normalized AS (
    SELECT * FROM {{ ref('int__invoice_items_with_normalized_fields') }}
),

-- Look up the previous valid purchase per (item, vendor). Voided rows and rows
-- with non-positive cost are excluded so they don't pollute the comparison
-- window. This mirrors `item_price_data → price_comparison` in
-- `mart__price_increases.sql`. The ORDER BY is intentionally only on `date`
-- (no `invoice_items_id` tiebreaker) so this model produces the *same*
-- previous_cost / previous_qty / rerating decisions as `mart__price_increases`
-- for rows on the same date. Adding a deterministic tiebreaker here would
-- silently diverge the two implementations on tied dates (~47k rows in prod),
-- which defeats the goal of issue #899.
valid_purchase_history AS (
    SELECT
        invoice_items_id,
        LAG(cost) OVER (
            PARTITION BY item, vendor
            ORDER BY "date" ASC
        ) AS previous_cost,
        LAG(qty) OVER (
            PARTITION BY item, vendor
            ORDER BY "date" ASC
        ) AS previous_qty,
        LAG("date") OVER (
            PARTITION BY item, vendor
            ORDER BY "date" ASC
        ) AS previous_date
    FROM normalized
    WHERE cost IS NOT NULL
      AND cost > 0
      AND invoice_voided_at IS NULL
),

-- Stitch previous-purchase context back onto every row (including voided /
-- zero-cost ones, which receive NULL previous_*) and flag rerating candidates.
flagged AS (
    SELECT
        n.*,
        vp.previous_cost,

model.mpi_analytics.int__invoice_items_w.compiled_code:
/*
Invoice Items with Rerated Pricing

Adds Y & S (BOX vs EACH UOM mismatch) price rerating on top of the normalized
intermediate. Downstream marts that need rerated cost/qty (Data Review, Price
Changes, QuickBooks, Mapping, Purchase Order, Supplier Comparison) should source
from this model instead of `int__invoice_items_with_normalized_fields`.

What this model adds vs upstream:
  - previous_cost, previous_qty, previous_date  (LAG by item+vendor, date ASC)
  - is_price_rerated                            (TRUE when threshold tripped for Y&S)
  - rerated_cost, rerated_qty                   (corrected EACH-equivalent values)
  - original_current_price, original_current_qty (= cost / qty, kept for clarity)

The detection and correction rules are kept in lock-step with the equivalent
CTEs in `mart__price_increases.sql`. Voided rows and rows with non-positive
cost are excluded from the LAG window (matching `mart__price_increases`) so
they neither receive a `previous_cost` nor anchor one for later rows.

Detection rule:
  vendor = 'Y & S Plumbing Supply'
  AND previous_cost IS NOT NULL AND previous_cost > 0
  AND ((cost - previous_cost) / previous_cost * 100) > price_increase_threshold

Correction rule (preserves total spend cost*qty):
  ratio          = ROUND(cost / previous_cost)
  rerated_cost   = ROUND((cost / NULLIF(ratio, 0))::numeric, 2)
  rerated_qty    = qty  * NULLIF(ratio, 0)

The raw `cost` and `qty` columns are preserved unchanged so consumers can choose
which value to expose. Columns are additive.

Materialization:
  Full-refresh table. The LAG window requires the complete history per
  (item, vendor) pair, so we rebuild from scratch each run (mirrors the strategy
  used by `mart__price_increases`). Cost is amortized across all downstream marts.

Lineage:
  int__invoice_items_mapped
    → int__invoice_items_with_normalized_fields
      → THIS MODEL
        → mart__invoice_items, mart__invoice_items_map,
          mart__item_price_comparison, mart__mapping_audit,
          mart__address_sheet_aggregates
*/





WITH normalized AS (
    SELECT * FROM "mpi_db"."analytics_intermediate"."int__invoice_items_with_normalized_fields"
),

-- Look up the previous valid purchase per (item, vendor). Voided rows and rows
-- with non-positive cost are excluded so they don't pollute the comparison
-- window. This mirrors `item_price_data → price_comparison` in
-- `mart__price_increases.sql`. The ORDER BY is intentionally only on `date`
-- (no `invoice_items_id` tiebreaker) so this model produces the *same*
-- previous_cost / previous_qty / rerating decisions as `mart__price_increases`
-- for rows on the same date. Adding a deterministic tiebreaker here would
-- silently diverge the two implementations on tied dates (~47k rows in prod),
-- which defeats the goal of issue #899.
valid_purchase_history AS (
    SELECT
        invoice_items_id,
        LAG(cost) OVER (
            PARTITION BY item, vendor
            ORDER BY "date" ASC
        ) AS previous_cost,
        LAG(qty) OVER (
            PARTITION BY item, vendor
            ORDER BY "date" ASC
        ) AS previous_qty,
        LAG("date") OVER (
            PARTITION BY item, vendor
            ORDER BY "date" ASC
        ) AS previous_date
    FROM normalized
    WHERE cost IS NOT NULL
      AND cost > 0
      AND invoice_voided_at IS NULL
),

-- Stitch previous-purchase context back onto every row (including voided /
-- zero-cost ones, which receive NULL previous_*) and flag rerating candidates.
flagged AS (
    SELECT
        n.*,
        vp.previous_cost,
        vp.previous_qty,
        vp.previous_date,
        CASE
            WHEN n.vendor = 'Y & S Plumbing Supply'
                AND vp.previous_cost IS NOT NULL
                AND vp.previous_cost > 0
                AND n.cost IS NOT NULL
                AND n.cost > 0
                AND ((n.cost - vp.previous_cost) / vp.previous_cost * 100) > 250
            THEN TRUE
            ELSE FALSE
        END AS is_price_rerated
    FROM normalized n
    LEFT JOIN valid_purchase_history vp
        ON n.invoice_items_id = vp.invoice_items_id
),

-- Apply the rerating correction. NULLIF guards against a ratio that rounds to
-- 0 (would only happen if cost ≤ 0.5 × previous_cost, i.e. not actually a
-- rerating candidate, but kept defensively).
rerated AS (
    SELECT
        f.*,

        -- Aliases that match mart__price_increases' renamed columns (PR #906).
        -- Always equal to raw cost/qty; provided so the FE doesn't have to know
        -- which intermediate it sourced the row from.
        f.cost AS original_current_price,
        f.qty  AS original_current_qty,

    FROM flagged f
)

model.mpi_analytics.mart__price_increase.name: mart__price_increases
model.mpi_analytics.mart__price_increase.description:
Price increase analysis mart that tracks price changes over time for each item-vendor pair.

**Purpose:**
- Provides historical price comparison for invoice items
- Enables supplier-specific price tracking
- Supports price trend analysis and reporting

**Key Business Logic:**
- Compares each purchase with the immediately preceding purchase chronologically
- Price comparisons are supplier-specific (same item from different suppliers tracked separately)
- Only includes items with valid cost > 0
- First purchase for an item-vendor pair has NULL previous_price

**Price Rerating Logic (UOM Mismatches):**
- Some vendors (e.g., 'Y & S Plumbing Supply') items purchase occasionally switch between unit pricing (EACH) and bulk pricing (BOX).
- This results in massive suspected price hikes (e.g., >250%) which are actually Unit of Measure (UOM) mismatches.
- **Detection:** When a price increase exceeds the threshold for specific vendors, it is flagged as `is_price_rerated`.
- **Correction:** We divide the current price by the rounded price ratio to estimate the 'EACH' price and simultaneously multiply the quantity by the same ratio.
- **Result:** This maintains the total invoice amount while allowing for accurate purchase-over-purchase price comparison.
- The original values are preserved in `original_current_price` and `original_current_qty`.

**Relationship to mart__invoice_items:**
- One-to-one relationship via invoice_items_id
- This mart enriches invoice_items with price history context
- Can be joined to get full item details + price increase data

**Usage Examples:**
```sql
-- Get all items with price increases > 10%
SELECT * FROM mart__price_increases
WHERE percentage_increase > 10;

-- Get price history for specific item from specific vendor
SELECT * FROM mart__price_increases
WHERE item = 'ABC123' AND vendor = 'Vendor Name'
ORDER BY purchase_date;

-- Join with invoice items for full context
SELECT
    ii.item,
    ii.description,
    ii.vendor,
    ii.customer_job,
    pi.purchase_date,
    pi.current_price,
    pi.previous_price,
    pi.percentage_increase_formatted
FROM mart__invoice_items ii
JOIN mart__price_increases pi ON ii.invoice_items_id = pi.invoice_items_id
WHERE pi.has_previous_price = TRUE;
```

**Performance Notes:**
- Materialized as table for fast query performance
- Indexed on common query patterns (item, vendor, date)
- Composite index on (item, vendor) for supplier-specific queries
- ANALYZE post-hook ensures query planner has fresh statistics

invoice_items_id.name: invoice_items_id
invoice_items_id.description:
Unique identifier for the invoice item, foreign key to mart__invoice_items.
This creates a one-to-one relationship between the two marts.

item.name: item
item.description:
Item code/number from the invoice.
Used for grouping price history by product.

vendor.name: vendor
vendor.description:
Vendor/supplier name.
Critical for supplier-specific price tracking.

purchase_date.name: purchase_date
purchase_date.description:
Date of the current purchase.
Used for chronological ordering and temporal analysis.
Note: Renamed from 'current_date' to avoid conflict with PostgreSQL's CURRENT_DATE function.

current_price.name: current_price
current_price.description:
Unit price (cost) for the current purchase.
For specific vendors, this may be rerated if a large price increase suggests a UOM mismatch (e.g. BOX vs EACH).
See `is_price_rerated` and `original_current_price` for more details.

current_qty.name: current_qty
current_qty.description:
Quantity purchased in the current transaction.
Provided for context but not used in price comparison calculations.
For specific vendors, this may be rerated if a large price increase suggests a UOM mismatch.
See `is_price_rerated` and `original_current_qty` for more details.

previous_price.name: previous_price
previous_price.description:
Unit price (cost) from the immediately preceding purchase of this item from this vendor.
NULL if this is the first purchase for this item-vendor pair.

previous_date.name: previous_date
previous_date.description:
Date of the previous purchase.
NULL if this is the first purchase for this item-vendor pair.

previous_qty.name: previous_qty
previous_qty.description:
Quantity purchased in the previous transaction.
Provided for context.

percentage_increase.name: percentage_increase
percentage_increase.description:
Percentage change from previous_price to current_price, rounded to 1 decimal place.
Formula: ((current_price - previous_price) / previous_price * 100)
NULL if no previous price exists or previous_price = 0.
Negative values indicate price decreases.
Note: Uses the rerated `current_price` where applicable.

price_change.name: price_change
price_change.description:
Absolute price change from previous_price to current_price (in dollars).
Formula: (current_price - previous_price)
NULL if no previous price exists.
Negative values indicate price decreases.
Note: Uses the rerated `current_price` where applicable.

has_previous_price.name: has_previous_price
has_previous_price.description:
Boolean flag indicating whether this item-vendor pair has price history.
TRUE: This item has been purchased before from this vendor
FALSE: This is the first purchase for this item-vendor pair

is_price_rerated.name: is_price_rerated
is_price_rerated.description:
Boolean flag indicating whether the current_price was rerated due to a suspected UOM mismatch.
See model description for detailed rerating logic.

original_current_price.name: original_current_price
original_current_price.description:
The original unit price (cost) before any rerating.
Matches `current_price` if `is_price_rerated` is FALSE.

original_current_qty.name: original_current_qty
original_current_qty.description:
The original quantity before any rerating.
Matches `current_qty` if `is_price_rerated` is FALSE.

percentage_increase_formatted.name: percentage_increase_formatted
percentage_increase_formatted.description:
Human-readable percentage string with '%' suffix or 'N/A'.
Examples: '15.5%', '-10.2%', 'N/A'
Matches the output format of the original calculate_price_increase method.

model.mpi_analytics.mart__price_increase.raw_code:
-- Mart model for price increase analysis per invoice item.
-- Calculates percentage price increase by comparing each purchase with the previous purchase chronologically.
-- Supplier-specific: Compares prices within the same supplier only.
-- See mart__price_increases.yml for detailed documentation.

{% set price_increase_threshold = var('price_increase_threshold') %}

{{
    config(
        materialized='table',
        tags=['analysis', 'pricing', 'reporting'],
        indexes=[
            {'columns': ['invoice_items_id'], 'unique': True},
            {'columns': ['item']},
            {'columns': ['vendor']},
            {'columns': ['item', 'vendor']},
            {'columns': ['purchase_date']}
        ],
        post_hook=[
            "ANALYZE {{ this }}"
        ]
    )
}}

{#
  Price Increase Analysis Model:

  Purpose:
  - Tracks price changes for items over time, supplier-specific
  - Each row represents an invoice item purchase with its price comparison
  - Enables quick identification of price increases/decreases

  Key Features:
  - Supplier-specific comparison (same item from different suppliers tracked separately)
  - Chronological comparison (each purchase compared to immediately preceding purchase)
  - Handles edge cases (first purchase, missing prices, zero prices)
  - Price Rerating: For specific vendors (e.g., Y & S Plumbing Supply), large price hikes ( > price_increase_threshold)
    are treated as UOM mismatches (BOX vs EACH) and rerated for accurate comparison.

  Indexes:
  1. invoice_items_id (unique) - Primary key linking to mart__invoice_items
  2. item - Item code filtering
  3. vendor - Supplier filtering
  4. (item, vendor) - Composite for supplier-specific item queries
  5. purchase_date - Temporal analysis

  Business Rules:
  - Only compares items with valid cost > 0 (zero-cost items excluded)
  - Comparison is per-supplier (same item from different suppliers tracked independently)
  - First purchase for item-vendor pair has NULL previous_price
  - Zero previous prices result in NULL percentage_increase to avoid division errors
  - Price Rerating: If percentage increase > price_increase_threshold for "Y & S Plumbing Supply",
    the current price is rerated: current_price = current_price / ROUND(current_price / previous_price)
  - Must maintain 1-to-1 parity with InvoiceItems.calculate_price_increase() controller method
#}

WITH item_price_data AS (
    -- Source: Get all active invoice items with valid pricing information
    -- WHY: We need clean, filtered data with only items that have valid costs
    SELECT
        invoice_items_id,
        item,
        vendor,
        "date",  -- Quoted because date is a reserved keyword in PostgreSQL
        cost AS COST,
        qty
    FROM {{ ref('int__invoice_items_with_normalized_fields') }}
    WHERE cost IS NOT NULL
        AND cost > 0
        AND invoice_voided_at IS NULL
),

price_comparison AS (
    -- Calculate price changes using window functions for efficient chronological comparison
    -- WHY: LAG function allows us to compare each purchase with the immediately preceding one
    --      within the same item-vendor partition
    SELECT
        ipd.invoice_items_id,
        ipd.item,
        ipd.vendor,
        ipd."date",
        ipd.cost AS current_price,
        ipd.qty AS current_qty,

        -- Get previous price and date for the same item from the same vendor
        LAG(ipd.cost) OVER (
            PARTITION BY ipd.item, ipd.vendor
            ORDER BY ipd."date" ASC
        ) AS previous_price,

        LAG(ipd."date") OVER (
            PARTITION BY ipd.item, ipd.vendor
            ORDER BY ipd."date" ASC
        ) AS previous_date,

        LAG(ipd.qty) OVER (
            PARTITION BY ipd.item, ipd.vendor
            ORDER BY ipd."date" ASC
        ) AS previous_qty
    FROM item_price_data ipd
),

price_rerating AS (
    -- Identify suspected UOM mismatches for specific vendors
    -- WHY: Some vendors switch between BOX and EACH pricing, causing massive percentage hikes (>250%).
    --      We flag these for rerating to ensure meaningful price comparisons.
    SELECT
        pc.*,
        CASE
            WHEN pc.vendor = 'Y & S Plumbing Supply'
                AND pc.previous_price IS NOT NULL
                AND pc.previous_price > 0
                AND ((pc.current_price - pc.previous_price) / pc.previous_price * 100) > {{ price_increase_threshold }}
            THEN TRUE
            ELSE FALSE
        END AS is_price_rerated
    FROM price_comparison pc
),

final_price_data AS (
    -- Apply price and qty rerating if the mismatch flag is set
    -- WHY: If rerated, we divide the current price by the rounded price ratio to get the 'EACH' price.
    --      Simultaneously, we multiply the quantity by the same ratio to keep the total amount consistent.
    --      We round the final price to 2 decimal places for consistency.
    SELECT
        pr.*,
        ROUND(
            (CASE
                WHEN pr.is_price_rerated THEN
                    pr.current_price / NULLIF(ROUND(pr.current_price / pr.previous_price), 0)
                ELSE pr.current_price
            END)::numeric,
            2
        ) AS final_current_price,
        CASE
            WHEN pr.is_price_rerated THEN
                pr.current_qty * NULLIF(ROUND(pr.current_price / pr.previous_price), 0)
            ELSE pr.current_qty
        END AS final_current_qty
    FROM price_rerating pr
),

price_increase_calc AS (
    -- Calculate percentage increase with proper handling of edge cases
    -- WHY: Need to handle NULL and zero previous prices to avoid division errors.
    --      Calculations are based on the final (possibly rerated) current price.
    SELECT
        fpd.invoice_items_id,
        fpd.item,
        fpd.vendor,
        fpd."date" AS purchase_date,
        fpd.final_current_price AS current_price,
        fpd.final_current_qty AS current_qty,
        fpd.previous_price,
        fpd.previous_date,
        fpd.previous_qty,
        fpd.is_price_rerated,
        fpd.current_price AS original_current_price, -- Original price before rerating
        fpd.current_qty AS original_current_qty, -- Original qty before rerating

        -- Calculate percentage increase
        CASE
            WHEN fpd.previous_price IS NULL THEN NULL  -- First purchase, no comparison
            WHEN fpd.previous_price = 0 THEN NULL      -- Avoid division by zero
            ELSE ROUND(
                ((fpd.final_current_price - fpd.previous_price) / fpd.previous_price * 100)::numeric,
                1
            )
        END AS percentage_increase,

        -- Calculate absolute price change
        CASE
            WHEN fpd.previous_price IS NULL THEN NULL
            ELSE ROUND((fpd.final_current_price - fpd.previous_price)::numeric, 2)
        END AS price_change,

        -- Flag for whether this item has price history
        CASE
            WHEN fpd.previous_price IS NOT NULL THEN TRUE
            ELSE FALSE
        END AS has_previous_price

    FROM final_price_data fpd
)

SELECT
    invoice_items_id,
    item,
    vendor,
    purchase_date,
    current_price,
    current_qty,
    previous_price,
    previous_date,
    previous_qty,
    percentage_increase,
    price_change,
    has_previous_price,
    is_price_rerated,
    original_current_price,
    original_current_qty,

    -- Add formatted percentage string for easy display (matching original method output)
    CASE
        WHEN percentage_increase IS NOT NULL THEN
            CAST(percentage_increase AS TEXT) || '%'
        ELSE 'N/A'
    END AS percentage_increase_formatted

FROM price_increase_calc

model.mpi_analytics.int__invoice_items_w.raw_code:
/*
Invoice Items with Normalized Fields

Adds normalization and account assignment logic on top of mapped invoice items.
This is the final intermediate layer before mart models.

Data lineage:
  stg__invoice_items → int__invoice_items → int__invoice_items_mapped → THIS MODEL → marts

Incremental Strategy:
  - MERGE on invoice_items_id, cascading from int__invoice_items_mapped via _dbt_updated_at
  - Detects: upstream changes (mapped model), user override additions/updates/removals
  - Post-hook DELETE handles re-extractions: removes rows whose invoice_items_id no longer
    exists in the upstream mapped table (orphaned by re-extraction ID changes)

*/

{{ config(
    materialized='incremental',
    unique_key='invoice_items_id',
    incremental_strategy='merge',
    on_schema_change='sync_all_columns',
    schema='intermediate',
    indexes=[
        {'columns': ['invoice_items_id'], 'unique': True},
        {'columns': ['item', 'vendor']},
        {'columns': ['is_active']},
        {'columns': ['_dbt_updated_at']},
        {'columns': ['is_overridden']},
        {'columns': ['invoice_voided_at']}
    ],
    post_hook=[
        "{% if not is_incremental() %}ANALYZE {{ this }}{% endif %}",
        "{% if is_incremental() %}DELETE FROM {{ this }} t WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM {{ ref('int__invoice_items_mapped') }} m WHERE m.invoice_items_id = t.invoice_items_id){% endif %}"
    ]
) }}

WITH mapped_items AS (
    SELECT * FROM {{ ref('int__invoice_items_mapped') }}
),

buyers_normalized AS (
    SELECT * FROM {{ ref('int__buyers') }}
),

vendors_normalized AS (
    SELECT * FROM {{ ref('int__vendors') }}
),

user_overrides AS (
    SELECT * FROM {{ ref('int__user_overrides') }}
),

invoice_voided AS (
    SELECT * FROM {{ source('public', 'invoice_voided') }}
),

{% if is_incremental() %}
-- Anchor the incremental watermark once so every change detector compares against
-- the same cut-off for this run.
last_run AS (
    SELECT COALESCE(MAX(_dbt_updated_at), '1900-01-01'::timestamp) AS max_ts
    FROM {{ this }}
),

changed_from_mapped AS (
    -- Why: upstream mapped rows changed (new extraction/mapping updates).
    -- Filter: only ids newer than this model's latest _dbt_updated_at.
    SELECT m.invoice_items_id
    FROM mapped_items m
    CROSS JOIN last_run lr
    WHERE m._dbt_updated_at > lr.max_ts
),

changed_from_override_upserts AS (
    -- Why: user created or edited overrides after last run.
    -- Filter:
    --   1) overridden_at > max_ts (recent override activity)
    --   2) numeric record_id only (safe bigint cast)
    --   3) id must exist in mapped_items (skip orphan/non-mapped override rows)
    SELECT m.invoice_items_id
    FROM user_overrides ov
    JOIN mapped_items m
        ON m.invoice_items_id::text = ov.record_id
    CROSS JOIN last_run lr
    WHERE ov.overridden_at > lr.max_ts
      AND ov.record_id ~ '^[0-9]+$'
),

previously_overridden AS (
    -- Snapshot of ids this model currently marks as overridden.
    SELECT t.invoice_items_id
    FROM {{ this }} t
    WHERE t.is_overridden = TRUE
),

currently_overridden AS (
    -- Snapshot of ids currently present in active override records.
    SELECT m.invoice_items_id
    FROM user_overrides ov
    JOIN mapped_items m
        ON m.invoice_items_id::text = ov.record_id
    WHERE ov.record_id ~ '^[0-9]+$'
),

changed_from_override_removals AS (
    -- Why: override was removed/reverted since last run.
    -- Filter: ids that were overridden before but are no longer in current overrides.
    SELECT p.invoice_items_id
    FROM previously_overridden p
    LEFT JOIN currently_overridden c
        ON p.invoice_items_id = c.invoice_items_id
    WHERE c.invoice_items_id IS NULL
),

changed_from_void_state AS (
    -- Why: void status changed and must be re-materialized.
    -- Branch A: newly voided now (exists in invoice_voided now, but target row was not voided).
    -- Branch B: restored now (target row was voided, but no longer matches invoice_voided join).
    SELECT m.invoice_items_id
    FROM mapped_items m
    JOIN invoice_voided iv
        ON m.ref_no = iv.ref_no
       AND m.date   = iv.date
       AND m.vendor = iv.vendor
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM {{ this }} t
        WHERE t.invoice_items_id = m.invoice_items_id
          AND t.invoice_voided_at IS NOT NULL
    )

    UNION

    SELECT t.invoice_items_id
    FROM {{ this }} t
    WHERE t.invoice_voided_at IS NOT NULL
      AND NOT EXISTS (
          SELECT 1
          FROM mapped_items m
          JOIN invoice_voided iv
              ON m.ref_no = iv.ref_no
             AND m.date   = iv.date
             AND m.vendor = iv.vendor
          WHERE m.invoice_items_id = t.invoice_items_id
      )
),

changed_invoice_items AS (
    -- Final incremental workset. UNION de-duplicates ids touched by multiple change signals.
    SELECT invoice_items_id FROM changed_from_mapped
    UNION
    SELECT invoice_items_id FROM changed_from_override_upserts
    UNION
    SELECT invoice_items_id FROM changed_from_override_removals
    UNION
    SELECT invoice_items_id FROM changed_from_void_state
),
{% endif %}

-- Compute effective field values by merging user overrides on top of mart values.
-- All downstream expressions MUST reference effective_* columns so that overrides
-- propagate consistently to assigned_account, corrected_amount, and normalized search
-- columns.  Numeric casts are guarded by a regex check to prevent cast failures when
-- a user submits a non-numeric string.
effective_values AS (
    SELECT
        m.*,
        COALESCE(ov.mpi_item,        m.resolved_mpi_item)        AS effective_mpi_item,
        COALESCE(ov.mpi_description, m.resolved_mpi_description) AS effective_mpi_description,
        COALESCE(ov.sheet_name,      m.resolved_sheet_name)      AS effective_sheet_name,
        COALESCE(ov.account,         m.account)                  AS effective_account,
        COALESCE(ov.memo,            m.memo)                     AS effective_memo,
        COALESCE(ov.description,     m.description)              AS effective_description,
        COALESCE(ov.qty,             m.qty)                      AS effective_qty,
        COALESCE(ov.customer_job,    m.customer_job)             AS effective_customer_job,
        COALESCE(ov.date,            m.date)                     AS effective_date,
        COALESCE(ov.vendor,          m.vendor)                   AS effective_vendor,
        COALESCE(ov.po_number,       m.po_number)                AS effective_po_number,
        COALESCE(ov.buyer,           m.buyer)                    AS effective_buyer,
        COALESCE(ov.class_,          m.class_)                   AS effective_class_,
        COALESCE(ov.cost,            m.cost)                     AS effective_cost,
        COALESCE(ov.amount,          m.amount)                   AS effective_amount,
        CASE WHEN ov.record_id IS NOT NULL THEN TRUE ELSE FALSE END AS is_overridden,
        ov.customer_job IS NOT NULL AS is_customer_job_overridden,
        ov.overridden_by,
        ov.overridden_at,
        iv.invoice_voided_at,
        normalize_address_fn(COALESCE(ov.customer_job, m.customer_job)) AS _addr_pre_normalized
    FROM mapped_items m
    {% if is_incremental() %}
    -- On incremental runs, only process ids identified by changed_invoice_items.
    -- This avoids scanning/normalizing the full mapped table on every run.
    INNER JOIN changed_invoice_items ci
        ON ci.invoice_items_id = m.invoice_items_id
    {% endif %}
    LEFT JOIN user_overrides ov
        ON m.invoice_items_id::text = ov.record_id
    LEFT JOIN invoice_voided iv
        ON m.ref_no = iv.ref_no
       AND m.date   = iv.date
       AND m.vendor = iv.vendor
),

with_normalization AS (
    SELECT
        -- Pass through all columns from mapped_items
        e.invoice_items_id,
        e.filename,
        e.item,
        e.effective_description     AS description,
        e.effective_mpi_item        AS resolved_mpi_item,
        e.effective_mpi_description AS resolved_mpi_description,
        e.effective_sheet_name      AS resolved_sheet_name,
        e.effective_qty             AS qty,
        e.effective_cost            AS cost,
        e.effective_amount          AS amount,
        e.effective_date            AS date,
        e.ref_no,
        e.effective_po_number       AS po_number,
        e.effective_customer_job    AS customer_job,
        -- Vendor: use canonical supplier name if matched, otherwise original
        COALESCE(vn.matched_supplier_fuzzy, e.effective_vendor) AS vendor,
        e.vendor AS vendor_raw,
        e.effective_buyer           AS buyer,
        e.date_added,
        e.invoice_id,
        e.matched_supplier,
        e.matched_supplier_id,
        e.is_active,
        e.mapping_type,
        e.mapping_source,
        e.mapped_at,
        e.original_mpi_item,
        e.original_mpi_description,
        e.original_sheet_name,
        e.effective_account AS account,
        e.is_overridden,
        e.is_customer_job_overridden,
        e.overridden_by,
        e.overridden_at,

        -- Address normalization (pre-computed in effective_values to avoid 17× function re-evaluation)
        {{ normalize_address('e.effective_customer_job', precomputed_column='e._addr_pre_normalized') }} AS customer_job_normalized,
        e.customer_job AS original_customer_job,

        -- Sheet name normalization (using effective_sheet_name)
        {{ normalize_sheet_name('e.effective_sheet_name') }} AS sheet_name_normalized,

        -- Buyer normalization (from join)
        e.buyer AS original_buyer,
        bn.buyer_normalized_base,
        bn.buyer_normalized_canonical,

        -- Vendor normalization metadata (from fuzzy matching join)
        vn.matched_supplier_id_fuzzy AS vendor_supplier_id,
        vn.similarity_score AS vendor_match_score,

        -- Account assignment (uses effective values so overrides propagate)
        CASE
            -- 1. Preserve explicit 'A'
            WHEN UPPER(e.effective_account) = 'A' THEN 'A'
            -- 2. UIDI-specific mapping using effective mpi_item
            WHEN e.effective_mpi_item = 'UIDI - Job Materials Purchased' THEN 'M'
            WHEN e.effective_mpi_item = 'UIDI - Job Equipment' THEN 'E'
            -- 3. Fallback to sheet_name patterns
            WHEN LOWER(e.effective_sheet_name) LIKE '%job materials%' THEN 'M'
            WHEN LOWER(e.effective_sheet_name) LIKE '%job equipment%' THEN 'E'
            -- 4. Fallback to original account if it exists
            WHEN e.effective_account IS NOT NULL AND e.effective_account != '' THEN e.effective_account
            -- 5. Default to NULL if no rule applies
            ELSE NULL
        END AS assigned_account,

        -- Corrected amount (for credit memos, uses effective amount)
        CASE
            WHEN e.ref_no LIKE 'CR-%' THEN -ABS(e.effective_amount)
            ELSE e.effective_amount
        END AS corrected_amount,

        -- Reference number normalized (for dedup)
        CASE
            WHEN REGEXP_LIKE(e.ref_no, '^[A-Za-z]+-0+[0-9]+$')
                THEN SPLIT_PART(e.ref_no, '-', 1) || '-' || LTRIM(SPLIT_PART(e.ref_no, '-', 2), '0')
            WHEN REGEXP_LIKE(e.ref_no, '^0+[0-9]+[A-Za-z]+$')
                THEN LTRIM(e.ref_no, '0')
            WHEN REGEXP_LIKE(e.ref_no, '^[A-Za-z]+0+[0-9]+$')
                THEN REGEXP_REPLACE(e.ref_no, '([A-Za-z])0+', '\1')
            WHEN REGEXP_LIKE(e.ref_no, '^[0-9]+$')
                THEN LTRIM(e.ref_no, '0')
            ELSE e.ref_no
        END AS ref_no_normalized,

        -- Void state (from public.invoice_voided)
        e.invoice_voided_at,

        -- Keep additional fields for reference
        e.effective_class_  AS class_,
        e.bill,
        e.export_status,
        e.effective_memo AS memo,
        e.line_order,

        -- ============================================================================
        -- NORMALIZED COLUMNS FOR FUZZY SEARCH
        -- Pre-computed to eliminate expensive runtime REGEXP_REPLACE() calls
        -- ============================================================================

        -- Item columns (using effective values where appropriate)
        REGEXP_REPLACE(LOWER(SUBSTRING(e.item, 1, 1000)), '[-_\s\(\)]+', ' ', 'g') AS item_normalized,
        REGEXP_REPLACE(LOWER(SUBSTRING(COALESCE(e.effective_mpi_item, e.item), 1, 1000)), '[-_\s\(\)]+', ' ', 'g') AS mpi_item_normalized,

        -- Description columns
        REGEXP_REPLACE(LOWER(SUBSTRING(e.effective_description, 1, 1000)), '[-_\s\(\)]+', ' ', 'g') AS description_normalized,
        REGEXP_REPLACE(LOWER(SUBSTRING(COALESCE(e.effective_mpi_description, e.effective_description), 1, 1000)), '[-_\s\(\)]+', ' ', 'g') AS mpi_description_normalized,

        -- Vendor (pre-computed for fuzzy text search)
        REGEXP_REPLACE(LOWER(SUBSTRING(e.effective_vendor, 1, 1000)), '[-_\s\(\)]+', ' ', 'g') AS vendor_search_normalized,

        -- Buyer (uses normalized buyer from joined buyers model for fuzzy search)
        REGEXP_REPLACE(LOWER(SUBSTRING(bn.buyer_normalized_base, 1, 1000)), '[-_\s\(\)]+', ' ', 'g') AS buyer_normalized,

        -- Sheet name fuzzy (uses effective_sheet_name)
        REGEXP_REPLACE(
            LOWER(
                SUBSTRING(
                    {{ normalize_sheet_name('e.effective_sheet_name') }},
                    1, 1000
                )
            ),
            '[-_\s\(\)]+', ' ', 'g'
        ) AS sheet_name_normalized_fuzzy,

        -- Account normalized (uses effective_account)
        REGEXP_REPLACE(LOWER(SUBSTRING(e.effective_account, 1, 1000)), '[-_\s\(\)]+', ' ', 'g') AS account_normalized,

        -- PO Number
        REGEXP_REPLACE(LOWER(SUBSTRING(e.effective_po_number, 1, 1000)), '[-_\s\(\)]+', ' ', 'g') AS po_number_normalized,

        -- Export status
        REGEXP_REPLACE(LOWER(SUBSTRING(e.export_status, 1, 1000)), '[-_\s\(\)]+', ' ', 'g') AS export_status_normalized,

        CURRENT_TIMESTAMP AS _dbt_updated_at

    FROM effective_values e
    LEFT JOIN buyers_normalized bn
        ON e.effective_buyer = bn.buyer
    LEFT JOIN vendors_normalized vn
        ON e.effective_vendor = vn.vendor
)

This is the final intermediate layer before mart models.

model.mpi_analytics.int__buyers.name: int__buyers
model.mpi_analytics.int__buyers.description:
Intermediate model for buyer normalization and explicit mapping.

This model processes all distinct buyer names from invoice items and applies:
1. Normalization (title case, remove spaces and non-alphanumeric characters)
2. Explicit mapping via buyer_typo_map.sql macro

**Key Transformations:**
  - Removes all non-alphanumeric characters (including spaces)
  - Separates alphabetic and numeric segments
  - Formats as Title Case "Alphabetic Numeric" (first letter uppercase, rest lowercase)
  - Applies explicit mappings from buyer_typo_map.sql for deterministic results

**Business Logic:**
  The mapped buyer name is determined using explicit mappings first, then a safe auto-rollup:
  
  1. Normalize buyer name (title case, remove spaces, etc.) → `buyer_normalized_base`
  2. Look up in `buyer_typo_map.sql` for explicit mapping
  3. If found, use mapped canonical
  4. Otherwise, auto-canonicalize truncated numeric suffixes when safe:
     - Same alphabetic portion (e.g., "Christian")
     - Digits are a prefix of another buyer's digits (e.g., "347772" → "34777254")
     - Prefers the most common longer value in the data
  5. If still no match, use normalized name as-is → `buyer_normalized_canonical`
  
  No fuzzy matching is performed; mappings are explicit + deterministic prefix-based rollups only.
  
  This consolidates variations like:
  - "ARLEM", "ARLEM 929", "ARLEM 929442955", "ARLEM 9294429558" → all map to "Arlem 9294429558" (via explicit map)
  - "ANTHONY" and "ANTNY" → map to "Anthony" (via explicit map)
  - "BATTY 9298667415" and "BETTY 9298667415" → map to "Betty 9298667415" (via explicit map)

**Examples:**
  - "AR LE M 9 29 44 2 -9 55 8" → normalized: "Arlem 9294429558"
  - "ARLEM 929 442-9558" → normalized: "Arlem 9294429558"
  - "Arlem(929) 442-955" → normalized: "Arlem 929442955"
  - "Modachi Dutech" → normalized: "Modachidutech" (spaces removed)
  - "ANTHONY" → normalized: "Anthony" → mapped: "Anthony"
  - "ANTNY" → normalized: "Antny" → mapped: "Anthony" (via explicit map)
  - "DAVIDW 3478048772" → normalized: "Davidw 3478048772"
  - "( 8 62 ) 3 18 - 00 7 4" → normalized: "8623180074"

buyer.name: buyer
buyer.description:
Original buyer name as it appears in the source data.
This is the raw, unmodified buyer value from invoice items.

buyer_normalized_base.name: buyer_normalized_base
buyer_normalized_base.description:
Normalized buyer name with consistent formatting.

Normalization process:
1. Remove all non-alphanumeric characters (including spaces)
2. Separate alphabetic and numeric segments
3. Format as Title Case "Alphabetic Numeric" (first letter uppercase, rest lowercase)
4. Add space separator between alphabetic and numeric parts if both exist

This provides a consistent representation for matching and grouping.

buyer_normalized_canonical.name: buyer_normalized_canonical
buyer_normalized_canonical.description:
Mapped (standardized) buyer name determined by explicit mapping from buyer_typo_map.sql.

For each normalized buyer, this field contains:
- The mapped canonical name if found in buyer_typo_map.sql
- Otherwise, an auto-canonicalized "best" value when the numeric suffix is clearly truncated
- Otherwise, the normalized buyer name itself (buyer_normalized_base)

All mappings are explicit and deterministic - no fuzzy matching is performed.

This helps consolidate variations of the same buyer under one canonical name.
For example:
- "Arlem", "Arlem 929", "Arlem 929442955", "Arlem 9294429558" → all map to "Arlem 9294429558" (via explicit map)
- "Anthony" and "Antny" → map to "Anthony" (via explicit map)

If no mapping is found, this equals buyer_normalized_base.

model.mpi_analytics.int__buyers.raw_code:
/* Intermediate model for buyer normalization and explicit mapping */

{{ config(
  materialized='view',
  schema='intermediate'
) }}

-- Source the buyer universe from the same switching layer the rest of the
-- pipeline uses (int__extracted_data_switched), instead of the old-pipeline-only
-- int__model_extracted_data. Otherwise distinct buyers that exist only in the
-- new normalized pipeline (int__extracted_data_combined_compat) are missing
-- here, the LEFT JOIN in int__invoice_items_with_normalized_fields fails for
-- those rows, buyer_normalized_canonical comes back NULL, and the mart's
-- `buyer` column (aliased from buyer_normalized_canonical) shows blank in the
-- data review page even though the raw extraction had the buyer value. (#870)
WITH distinct_buyers AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT
        buyer
    FROM {{ ref('int__extracted_data_switched') }}
    WHERE is_active = true
      AND buyer IS NOT NULL
      AND TRIM(buyer) != ''
),

buyer_counts AS (
    -- Count occurrences so auto-canonicalization prefers the most common "full" buyer value.
    SELECT
        buyer,
        COUNT(*)::bigint AS buyer_count
    FROM {{ ref('int__extracted_data_switched') }}
    WHERE is_active = true
      AND buyer IS NOT NULL
      AND TRIM(buyer) != ''
    GROUP BY buyer
),

normalized_buyers AS (
    -- Step 1: Normalize buyer into "Alpha Numeric" (Title Case alpha; digits grouped)
    -- Inline normalization logic (no function dependency)
    SELECT
        buyer AS original_buyer,
        CASE
            WHEN buyer IS NULL OR TRIM(buyer) = '' THEN buyer
            ELSE
                -- Remove all non-alphanumeric, then extract alpha and numeric parts
                CASE
                    WHEN REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(buyer, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^A-Za-z]', '', 'g') != ''
                         AND REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(buyer, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^0-9]', '', 'g') != ''
                    THEN
                        -- Format as "Alpha Numeric" with Title Case
                        INITCAP(REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(buyer, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^A-Za-z]', '', 'g')) || ' ' ||
                        REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(buyer, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^0-9]', '', 'g')
                    WHEN REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(buyer, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^A-Za-z]', '', 'g') != ''
                    THEN
                        INITCAP(REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(buyer, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^A-Za-z]', '', 'g'))
                    WHEN REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(buyer, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^0-9]', '', 'g') != ''
                    THEN
                        REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(buyer, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^0-9]', '', 'g')
                    ELSE ''
                END
        END AS buyer_normalized_base
    FROM distinct_buyers
),

normalized_buyers_enriched AS (
    SELECT
        nb.original_buyer,
        nb.buyer_normalized_base,
        REGEXP_REPLACE(COALESCE(nb.buyer_normalized_base, ''), '[^A-Za-z]', '', 'g') AS alpha_part,
        REGEXP_REPLACE(COALESCE(nb.buyer_normalized_base, ''), '[^0-9]', '', 'g') AS numeric_part,
        COALESCE(bc.buyer_count, 0)::bigint AS buyer_count
    FROM normalized_buyers nb
    LEFT JOIN buyer_counts bc
        ON bc.buyer = nb.original_buyer
),

buyer_typo_overrides_raw AS (
    {#-
      Flatten `buyer_typo_map()` into (canonical_raw, variant_raw) rows.
      This provides explicit, deterministic mappings for buyer name normalization.
    -#}
    {% set m = buyer_typo_map() %}
    {% set ns = namespace(rows=[]) %}
    {% for canonical, variants in m.items() %}
        {% for variant in variants %}
            {% set c_escaped = canonical | replace("'", "''") %}
            {% set v_escaped = variant | replace("'", "''") %}
            {% set row_str = "('" ~ c_escaped ~ "'::text, '" ~ v_escaped ~ "'::text)" %}
            {% set ns.rows = ns.rows + [row_str] %}
        {% endfor %}
    {% endfor %}
    {% if ns.rows | length == 0 %}
    SELECT NULL::text AS canonical_raw, NULL::text AS variant_raw WHERE FALSE
    {% else %}
    SELECT
        t.canonical_raw,
        t.variant_raw
    FROM (
        VALUES {{ ns.rows | join(', ') }}
    ) AS t(canonical_raw, variant_raw)
    {% endif %}
),

buyer_typo_overrides_norm AS (
    -- Normalize variants for matching, but KEEP canonical in display form (with spaces)
    -- This allows: "Mordchaideutch" -> "Mordchai Deutch" (display), even though the
    -- normalized key becomes "Mordchaideutch".
    --
    -- Also dedupe on variant_norm in case multiple raw variants collapse to the same norm.
    SELECT
        variant_norm,
        (ARRAY_AGG(canonical_display ORDER BY LENGTH(canonical_display) DESC))[1] AS canonical_display
    FROM buyer_typo_overrides_raw
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
        SELECT
            -- Inline normalization logic for variant_raw (no function dependency)
            CASE
                WHEN variant_raw IS NULL OR TRIM(variant_raw) = '' THEN variant_raw
                ELSE
                    CASE
                        WHEN REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(variant_raw, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^A-Za-z]', '', 'g') != ''
                             AND REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(variant_raw, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^0-9]', '', 'g') != ''
                        THEN
                            INITCAP(REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(variant_raw, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^A-Za-z]', '', 'g')) || ' ' ||
                            REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(variant_raw, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^0-9]', '', 'g')
                        WHEN REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(variant_raw, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^A-Za-z]', '', 'g') != ''
                        THEN
                            INITCAP(REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(variant_raw, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^A-Za-z]', '', 'g'))
                        WHEN REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(variant_raw, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^0-9]', '', 'g') != ''
                        THEN
                            REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(variant_raw, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^0-9]', '', 'g')
                        ELSE ''
                    END
            END AS variant_norm,
            TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(canonical_raw, '[[:space:]]+', ' ', 'g')) AS canonical_display
    ) x
    WHERE variant_raw IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(variant_raw) != ''
    GROUP BY variant_norm
),

mapped_buyers AS (
    -- Apply mapping AFTER normalization:
    -- 1) compute buyer_normalized_base
    -- 2) lookup mapping in buyer_typo_map.sql
    -- 3) if found -> mapped canonical
    -- 4) else auto-canonicalize truncated numeric suffixes (same alpha, digits are prefix of a longer digits value)
    -- 5) else -> buyer_normalized_base
    SELECT
        nb.original_buyer,
        nb.buyer_normalized_base,
        COALESCE(
            bo.canonical_display,
            ac.auto_canonical_base,
            nb.buyer_normalized_base
        ) AS buyer_normalized_canonical
    FROM normalized_buyers_enriched nb
    LEFT JOIN buyer_typo_overrides_norm bo
        ON bo.variant_norm = nb.buyer_normalized_base
    LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
        SELECT
            nb2.buyer_normalized_base AS auto_canonical_base
        FROM normalized_buyers_enriched nb2
        WHERE bo.canonical_display IS NULL  -- Only auto-canonicalize if no explicit mapping exists
          AND nb.alpha_part != ''
          AND nb.numeric_part != ''
          AND LENGTH(nb.numeric_part) >= 4  -- Only for buyers with at least 4 digits
          AND nb2.alpha_part = nb.alpha_part  -- Same name part
          AND nb2.numeric_part != ''
          AND nb2.numeric_part LIKE nb.numeric_part || '%'  -- nb's digits are a prefix of nb2's digits
          AND LENGTH(nb2.numeric_part) > LENGTH(nb.numeric_part)  -- nb2 has more digits (longer phone number)
        ORDER BY
            nb2.buyer_count DESC,  -- Prefer most common
            LENGTH(nb2.numeric_part) DESC,  -- Prefer longest phone number
            nb2.buyer_normalized_base
        LIMIT 1
    ) ac ON (bo.canonical_display IS NULL)  -- Only execute LATERAL join when no explicit mapping exists
)

SELECT
    original_buyer AS buyer,
    buyer_normalized_base,
    buyer_normalized_canonical
FROM mapped_buyers

buyer_typo_overrides_norm AS (
    -- Normalize variants for matching, but KEEP canonical in display form (with spaces)
    -- This allows: "Mordchaideutch" -> "Mordchai Deutch" (display), even though the
    -- normalized key becomes "Mordchaideutch".
    --
    -- Also dedupe on variant_norm in case multiple raw variants collapse to the same norm.
    SELECT
        variant_norm,
        (ARRAY_AGG(canonical_display ORDER BY LENGTH(canonical_display) DESC))[1] AS canonical_display
    FROM buyer_typo_overrides_raw
    CROSS JOIN LATERAL (
        SELECT
            -- Inline normalization logic for variant_raw (no function dependency)
            CASE
                WHEN variant_raw IS NULL OR TRIM(variant_raw) = '' THEN variant_raw
                ELSE
                    CASE
                        WHEN REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(variant_raw, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^A-Za-z]', '', 'g') != ''
                             AND REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(variant_raw, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^0-9]', '', 'g') != ''
                        THEN
                            INITCAP(REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(variant_raw, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^A-Za-z]', '', 'g')) || ' ' ||
                            REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(variant_raw, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^0-9]', '', 'g')
                        WHEN REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(variant_raw, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^A-Za-z]', '', 'g') != ''
                        THEN
                            INITCAP(REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(variant_raw, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^A-Za-z]', '', 'g'))
                        WHEN REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(variant_raw, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^0-9]', '', 'g') != ''
                        THEN
                            REGEXP_REPLACE(REGEXP_REPLACE(variant_raw, '[^A-Za-z0-9]', '', 'g'), '[^0-9]', '', 'g')
                        ELSE ''
                    END
            END AS variant_norm,
            TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(canonical_raw, '[[:space:]]+', ' ', 'g')) AS canonical_display
    ) x
    WHERE variant_raw IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(variant_raw) != ''
    GROUP BY variant_norm
),

mapped_buyers AS (
    -- Apply mapping AFTER normalization:
    -- 1) compute buyer_normalized_base
    -- 2) lookup mapping in buyer_typo_map.sql
    -- 3) if found -> mapped canonical
    -- 4) else auto-canonicalize truncated numeric suffixes (same alpha, digits are prefix of a longer digits value)
    -- 5) else -> buyer_normalized_base
    SELECT
        nb.original_buyer,
        nb.buyer_normalized_base,
        COALESCE(
            bo.canonical_display,
            ac.auto_canonical_base,
            nb.buyer_normalized_base
        ) AS buyer_normalized_canonical
    FROM normalized_buyers_enriched nb
    LEFT JOIN buyer_typo_overrides_norm bo
        ON bo.variant_norm = nb.buyer_normalized_base
    LEFT JOIN LATERAL (
        SELECT
            nb2.buyer_normalized_base AS auto_canonical_base
        FROM normalized_buyers_enriched nb2
        WHERE bo.canonical_display IS NULL  -- Only auto-canonicalize if no explicit mapping exists
          AND nb.alpha_part != ''
          AND nb.numeric_part != ''
          AND LENGTH(nb.numeric_part) >= 4  -- Only for buyers with at least 4 digits
          AND nb2.alpha_part = nb.alpha_part  -- Same name part
          AND nb2.numeric_part != ''
          AND nb2.numeric_part LIKE nb.numeric_part || '%'  -- nb's digits are a prefix of nb2's digits
          AND LENGTH(nb2.numeric_part) > LENGTH(nb.numeric_part)  -- nb2 has more digits (longer phone number)
        ORDER BY
            nb2.buyer_count DESC,  -- Prefer most common
            LENGTH(nb2.numeric_part) DESC,  -- Prefer longest phone number
            nb2.buyer_normalized_base
        LIMIT 1
    ) ac ON (bo.canonical_display IS NULL)  -- Only execute LATERAL join when no explicit mapping exists
)

SELECT
    original_buyer AS buyer,
    buyer_normalized_base,
    buyer_normalized_canonical
FROM mapped_buyers

model.mpi_analytics.int__vendors.raw_code:
/*
Intermediate model for vendor normalization using two-tier fuzzy matching.

Two-Tier Matching Strategy:
  TIER 1: Fuzzy match against vendor_variants_map() variants (0.6 threshold)
          Maps abbreviated/alternate names to canonical suppliers
  TIER 2: Direct fuzzy match against public.suppliers (0.7 threshold)
          Catches typos and minor variations

Example: "YS Plumbing LLC" → matches "YS Plumbing" variant → "Y & S Plumbing Supply"

Data lineage:
  int__invoice_items_mapped (vendor) + stg__suppliers + vendor_variants_map()
  → THIS MODEL → int__invoice_items_with_normalized_fields
*/

{{ config(
    materialized='view',
    schema='intermediate'
) }}

{# Flatten vendor variants map into (canonical, variant) rows #}
{%- set vendor_map = vendor_variants_map() -%}

WITH distinct_vendors AS (
    -- Get all distinct vendor values from mapped invoice items
    SELECT DISTINCT vendor
    FROM {{ ref('int__invoice_items_mapped') }}
    WHERE is_active = true
      AND vendor IS NOT NULL
      AND TRIM(vendor) != ''
),

suppliers AS (
    SELECT * FROM {{ ref('stg__suppliers') }}
),

-- Flatten the vendor variants map into rows
vendor_variants AS (
    {% for canonical, variants in vendor_map.items() %}
    {% for variant in variants %}
    SELECT '{{ canonical }}' AS canonical_supplier, '{{ variant }}' AS variant_key
    {% if not loop.last %}UNION ALL{% endif %}
    {% endfor %}
    {% if not loop.last %}UNION ALL{% endif %}
    {% endfor %}
),

-- TIER 1: Fuzzy match against variant keys (lower threshold since variants are explicit)
variant_matches AS (
    SELECT
        dv.vendor,
        vv.canonical_supplier,
        vv.variant_key AS matched_variant,
        SIMILARITY(LOWER(dv.vendor), LOWER(vv.variant_key)) AS variant_similarity,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY dv.vendor
            ORDER BY SIMILARITY(LOWER(dv.vendor), LOWER(vv.variant_key)) DESC
        ) AS variant_rank
    FROM distinct_vendors dv
    CROSS JOIN vendor_variants vv
    WHERE SIMILARITY(LOWER(dv.vendor), LOWER(vv.variant_key)) >= 0.6
),

-- TIER 2: Direct fuzzy match against suppliers (higher threshold for precision)
supplier_matches AS (
    SELECT
        dv.vendor,
        s.supplier_id,
        s.supplier_name,
        SIMILARITY(LOWER(dv.vendor), LOWER(s.supplier_name)) AS similarity_score,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY dv.vendor
            ORDER BY SIMILARITY(LOWER(dv.vendor), LOWER(s.supplier_name)) DESC
        ) AS match_rank
    FROM distinct_vendors dv
    CROSS JOIN suppliers s
    WHERE SIMILARITY(LOWER(dv.vendor), LOWER(s.supplier_name)) >= 0.7
)

SELECT
    dv.vendor,
    -- Priority: variant match > direct supplier match > original value
    COALESCE(
        vm.canonical_supplier,
        sm.supplier_name,
        dv.vendor
    ) AS vendor_normalized,
    -- Matched supplier info (for downstream use)
    COALESCE(vm.canonical_supplier, sm.supplier_name) AS matched_supplier_fuzzy,
    s.supplier_id AS matched_supplier_id_fuzzy,
    -- Match metadata
    CASE
        WHEN vm.canonical_supplier IS NOT NULL THEN vm.variant_similarity
        ELSE sm.similarity_score
    END AS similarity_score,
    CASE
        WHEN vm.canonical_supplier IS NOT NULL THEN 'variant'
        WHEN sm.supplier_name IS NOT NULL THEN 'direct'
        ELSE NULL
    END AS match_type,
    vm.matched_variant
FROM distinct_vendors dv
LEFT JOIN variant_matches vm
    ON dv.vendor = vm.vendor
    AND vm.variant_rank = 1
LEFT JOIN supplier_matches sm
    ON dv.vendor = sm.vendor
    AND sm.match_rank = 1
    AND vm.canonical_supplier IS NULL  -- Only use direct match if no variant match
LEFT JOIN suppliers s
    ON COALESCE(vm.canonical_supplier, sm.supplier_name) = s.supplier_name

model.mpi_analytics.int__invoice_items_m.description:
Intermediate Invoice Items with Resolved Mappings

Maps invoice line items to MPI items through priority-based matching:
1. Permanent mappings - supplier_item → mpi_code + mpi_description
2. Temporary mappings - supplier_item → sheet_name only → generates UIDI-{Job Equipment/Job Materials Purchased}
3. Possible match - no exact match, but possible matches found via suffix removal or case-insensitive matching
4. No match - item not found in any mapping → 'No Match'

**Data Quality:**
  - All invoice items have exactly one mapping (permanent, temporary, possible_match, or no_match)
  - Resolved MPI items are never null
  - Mapping type values are restricted to: permanent, temporary, possible_match, no_match

- Temporary mapping: generates UIDI-{Job Equipment/Job Materials Purchased}

mapping_type.description:
Type of mapping applied to this invoice item:
- permanent: Matched via permanent_mappings (supplier_item → mpi_code)
- temporary: Matched via temporary_mappings (supplier_item → sheet_name only)
- possible_match: No exact match, but possible matches found via suffix removal or case-insensitive matching
- no_match: No mapping found in either table

model.mpi_analytics.int__invoice_items_m.raw_code:
/*
Intermediate Invoice Items with Resolved Mappings

Maps invoice line items to MPI items through priority-based matching:
1. Permanent mappings - supplier_item → mpi_code + mpi_description
2. Temporary mappings - supplier_item → sheet_name only → generates UIDI-{Job Equipment/Job Materials Purchased}
3. Possible match - for unmatched items, suggests matches found by:
   a. Removing trailing suffix (-B, -Y pattern) from item code
   b. Case-insensitive matching
4. No match - item not found in any mapping → 'No Match'

Pipeline Switching:
  - Default: Uses old pipeline (int__model_extracted_data)
  - New pipeline: Run with --vars '{"data_source": "model_extracted_data"}'
    to use the new normalized pipeline (int__extracted_data_combined_compat)

Incremental Strategy:
  - MERGE on invoice_items_id (deterministic hash of extraction_id + invoice_index + line_order)
  - Detects: new invoices (date_added), mapping changes (extraction_timestamp vs _dbt_updated_at)
  - Post-hook DELETE handles re-extractions: when an invoice is re-extracted, it gets a new
    extraction_id → new invoice_items_id. The staging layer deletes old extraction rows, so the
    source view no longer contains the old IDs. The post-hook DELETE removes these orphaned rows
    from this table to prevent duplicate line items.

*/

{{ config(
    materialized='incremental',
    unique_key='invoice_items_id',
    incremental_strategy='merge',
    on_schema_change='sync_all_columns',
    schema='intermediate',
    indexes=[
        {'columns': ['invoice_items_id'], 'unique': True},
        {'columns': ['item']},
        {'columns': ['mapping_type']},
        {'columns': ['date_added']},
        {'columns': ['_dbt_updated_at']}
    ],
    post_hook=[
        "{% if not is_incremental() %}ANALYZE {{ this }}{% endif %}",
        "{% if is_incremental() %}DELETE FROM {{ this }} t WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM {{ ref('int__extracted_data_switched') }} s WHERE s.invoice_items_id = t.invoice_items_id){% endif %}"
    ]
) }}

-- Source invoice items
-- Uses switching model to support both old and new extraction pipelines
-- Note: mpi_item, mpi_description, sheet_name from PDF extraction are untrustworthy
-- They are kept as original_* columns for audit/comparison only
WITH invoice_items AS (
    SELECT
        invoice_items_id,
        filename,
        item,           -- Join key (supplier's item code from invoice)
        description,    -- Invoice description (used as fallback)
        vendor,
        date,
        ref_no,
        po_number,
        customer_job,
        buyer,
        date_added,
        invoice_id,
        class_,
        account,
        export_status,
        bill,
        memo,
        amount,
        cost,
        qty,
        is_active,
        -- Original values from PDF extraction (untrustworthy - for audit only)
        mpi_item AS original_mpi_item,
        mpi_description AS original_mpi_description,
        sheet_name AS original_sheet_name,
        line_order
    FROM {{ ref('int__extracted_data_switched') }}
    {% if is_incremental() %}
    WHERE
        -- 1. New invoice data: pick up rows added since last run (1-hour buffer for late arrivals)
        date_added > (SELECT COALESCE(MAX(date_added), '1900-01-01'::timestamp) - interval '1 hour' FROM {{ this }})
        -- 2. Permanent mapping changed: re-process items whose mapping was updated in Google Sheets
        OR invoice_items_id IN (
            SELECT t.invoice_items_id
            FROM {{ this }} t
            INNER JOIN {{ ref('int__permanent_mappings') }} pm
                ON TRIM(t.item) = TRIM(pm.supplier_item)
            WHERE pm.extraction_timestamp > t._dbt_updated_at
        )
        -- 3. Temporary mapping changed: same logic for temporary (sheet-only) mappings
        OR invoice_items_id IN (
            SELECT t.invoice_items_id
            FROM {{ this }} t
            INNER JOIN {{ ref('int__temporary_mappings') }} tm
                ON TRIM(t.item) = TRIM(tm.original_item)
            WHERE tm.extraction_timestamp > t._dbt_updated_at
        )
    {% endif %}
),

permanent_mappings AS (
    SELECT * FROM {{ ref('int__permanent_mappings') }}
),

temporary_mappings AS (
    SELECT * FROM {{ ref('int__temporary_mappings') }}
),

-- Step 1: Try permanent mapping (exact match on trimmed item codes)
with_permanent AS (
    SELECT
        i.*,
        p.mpi_code,
        p.mpi_description,
        p.sheet_name,
        p.supplier,
        p.supplier_id,
        p.mapping_source,
        p.extraction_timestamp AS perm_extraction_ts,
        CASE WHEN p.mpi_code IS NOT NULL THEN 'permanent' END AS match_type
    FROM invoice_items i
    LEFT JOIN permanent_mappings p
        ON LOWER(TRIM(i.item)) = LOWER(TRIM(p.supplier_item))
),

-- Step 2: Try temporary mapping if no permanent match found
with_fallback AS (
    SELECT
        wp.*,
        t.sheet_name AS temp_sheet_name,
        t.original_description AS temp_description,
        t.mapping_source AS temp_mapping_source,
        t.extraction_timestamp AS temp_extraction_ts,
        CASE
            WHEN wp.match_type = 'permanent' THEN 'permanent'
            WHEN t.original_item IS NOT NULL THEN 'temporary'
            ELSE 'no_match'
        END AS final_match_type
    FROM with_permanent wp
    LEFT JOIN temporary_mappings t
        ON TRIM(wp.item) = TRIM(t.original_item)
        AND wp.match_type IS NULL  -- Only attempt temp match if no permanent found
),

-- Step 3.a: Find possible matches via suffix removal (-B, -Y pattern)
suffix_possible AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (wf.invoice_items_id)
        wf.invoice_items_id,
        COALESCE(p.sheet_name, t.sheet_name) AS suffix_sheet_name,
        p.mpi_code AS suffix_possible_code
    FROM with_fallback wf
    LEFT JOIN permanent_mappings p
        ON TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(wf.item, '-[A-Za-z]$', '')) = TRIM(p.supplier_item)
    LEFT JOIN temporary_mappings t
        ON TRIM(REGEXP_REPLACE(wf.item, '-[A-Za-z]$', '')) = TRIM(t.original_item)
        AND p.mpi_code IS NULL
    WHERE wf.final_match_type = 'no_match'
      AND wf.item ~ '-[A-Za-z]$'
      AND (p.mpi_code IS NOT NULL OR t.sheet_name IS NOT NULL)
    ORDER BY wf.invoice_items_id, p.mpi_code NULLS LAST
),

    SELECT DISTINCT ON (wf.invoice_items_id)

        p.mpi_code AS case_possible_code
    FROM with_fallback wf
    LEFT JOIN permanent_mappings p
        ON UPPER(TRIM(wf.item)) = UPPER(TRIM(p.supplier_item))
        AND TRIM(wf.item) != TRIM(p.supplier_item)
    LEFT JOIN temporary_mappings t
        ON UPPER(TRIM(wf.item)) = UPPER(TRIM(t.original_item))
        AND TRIM(wf.item) != TRIM(t.original_item)
        AND p.mpi_code IS NULL
    WHERE wf.final_match_type = 'no_match'
      AND (p.mpi_code IS NOT NULL OR t.sheet_name IS NOT NULL)
    ORDER BY wf.invoice_items_id, p.mpi_code NULLS LAST
),

-- Step 4: Deduplicate to ensure one row per invoice item
-- (handles cases where multiple mappings match the same item)
with_dedup AS (
    SELECT
        *,
        ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
            PARTITION BY invoice_items_id
            ORDER BY
                -- Priority: permanent > temporary > no_match
                CASE final_match_type
                    WHEN 'permanent' THEN 1
                    WHEN 'temporary' THEN 2
                    ELSE 3
                END,
                -- Within same match type, prefer earlier mapping (deterministic)
                mpi_code NULLS LAST,
                temp_sheet_name NULLS LAST
        ) AS rn
    FROM with_fallback
),

-- Step 5: Resolve final values based on match priority
final AS (
    SELECT
        -- Identifiers
        wd.invoice_items_id,
        wd.filename,
        wd.item,
        wd.description,

        -- Resolved MPI values (priority: permanent > temporary > no_match)
        CASE wd.final_match_type
            WHEN 'permanent' THEN wd.mpi_code
            WHEN 'temporary' THEN {{ resolve_temp_mpi_item('wd.temp_sheet_name') }}
            ELSE
                CASE
                    WHEN sp.suffix_possible_code IS NOT NULL AND cp.case_possible_code IS NOT NULL
                         AND sp.suffix_possible_code != cp.case_possible_code
                    THEN 'Possible match: ' || sp.suffix_possible_code || ', ' || cp.case_possible_code
                    WHEN sp.suffix_possible_code IS NOT NULL
                    THEN 'Possible match: ' || sp.suffix_possible_code
                    WHEN cp.case_possible_code IS NOT NULL
                    THEN cp.case_possible_code
                    ELSE 'No Match'
                END
        END AS resolved_mpi_item,

        CASE wd.final_match_type
            WHEN 'permanent' THEN wd.mpi_description
            WHEN 'temporary' THEN COALESCE(wd.temp_description, wd.description)
            ELSE 'No Match'
        END AS resolved_mpi_description,

        CASE wd.final_match_type
            WHEN 'permanent' THEN wd.sheet_name
            WHEN 'temporary' THEN wd.temp_sheet_name
            ELSE COALESCE(sp.suffix_sheet_name, cp.case_sheet_name)
        END AS resolved_sheet_name,

        -- Financial data
        wd.qty,
        wd.cost,
        wd.amount,

        -- Invoice metadata
        wd.date,
        wd.ref_no,
        wd.po_number,
        wd.customer_job,
        wd.vendor,
        wd.buyer,
        wd.date_added,
        wd.invoice_id,

        -- Supplier info (from permanent mapping only)
        wd.supplier AS matched_supplier,
        wd.supplier_id AS matched_supplier_id,

        -- Status and additional fields
        wd.is_active,
        wd.class_,
        wd.account,
        wd.bill,
        wd.export_status,
        wd.memo,
        wd.line_order,

        -- Audit columns
        CASE
            WHEN wd.final_match_type = 'no_match'
                 AND (sp.suffix_possible_code IS NOT NULL OR cp.case_possible_code IS NOT NULL)
            THEN 'possible_match'
            ELSE wd.final_match_type
        END AS mapping_type,
        CASE
            WHEN wd.final_match_type = 'permanent' THEN wd.mapping_source
            WHEN wd.final_match_type = 'temporary' THEN wd.temp_mapping_source
            WHEN sp.suffix_possible_code IS NOT NULL OR cp.case_possible_code IS NOT NULL
            THEN 'possible_match'
            ELSE 'unmapped'
        END AS mapping_source,
        CURRENT_TIMESTAMP AS mapped_at,

        CASE wd.final_match_type
            WHEN 'permanent' THEN wd.perm_extraction_ts
            WHEN 'temporary' THEN wd.temp_extraction_ts
            ELSE NULL
        END AS _mapping_extraction_ts,
        CURRENT_TIMESTAMP AS _dbt_updated_at,

        -- Original values from PDF extraction (untrustworthy - for audit/comparison)
        wd.original_mpi_item,
        wd.original_mpi_description,
        wd.original_sheet_name

    FROM with_dedup wd
    LEFT JOIN suffix_possible sp ON wd.invoice_items_id = sp.invoice_items_id
    LEFT JOIN case_possible cp ON wd.invoice_items_id = cp.invoice_items_id
    WHERE wd.rn = 1
)
