test.mpi_analytics.assert_amount_sum_rec.name: assert_amount_sum_reconciliation
test.mpi_analytics.assert_amount_sum_rec.raw_code:
{{ config(tags=['reconciliation']) }}

/*
Test: Amount Reconciliation (Per-Row)
Description: For each staging row that matched to the mart (same invoice_items_id),
             compares the numeric amount at the row level. Excludes rows with known
             legitimate transformations:
             - Credit memo sign flips (CR- ref_no prefix)
             - User overrides that changed the amount
             - Non-parseable staging amounts (text that isn't a valid number)

             Returns individual rows where the staging and mart amounts differ by
             more than $0.01, indicating a data transformation issue.

Expected Result: 0 rows (test passes)
Failure Condition: Any matched row where the staging numeric amount differs
                   from the mart amount by more than $0.01.
*/

WITH matched AS (
    SELECT
        li.line_item_id,
        li.amount AS staging_amount_text,
        mart.amount AS mart_amount,
        mart.ref_no,
        mart.item,
        mart.vendor,
        mart.date
    FROM {{ ref('stg__extracted_line_items') }} li
    INNER JOIN {{ ref('mart__invoice_items') }} mart
        ON li.line_item_id = mart.invoice_items_id
    WHERE
        /*
          Defined in: int__extracted_data_combined and int__invoice_items_with_normalized_fields.
          Credit memos (ref_no starting with 'CR-') have their amount sign flipped to negative
          in the pipeline. The staging text has the original positive value, so these will
          always differ. Exclude from comparison.
        */
        mart.ref_no NOT LIKE 'CR-%'

        /*
          Defined in: int__invoice_items_with_normalized_fields (effective_values CTE).
          User overrides are stored in public.user_overrides as JSONB. When a user changes
          an amount via the app, the mart reflects the override but staging still has the
          original extraction value. Exclude these since the difference is intentional.
        */
        AND NOT EXISTS (
            SELECT 1 FROM {{ ref('int__user_overrides') }} uo
            WHERE uo.record_id = li.line_item_id::text
              AND uo.amount IS NOT NULL
        )

        /*
          Staging amounts are raw text from PDF extraction. Some aren't valid numbers
          (empty, malformed, or contain non-numeric characters). These can't be
          meaningfully compared, so we only check rows with parseable amounts.
        */
        AND li.amount ~ '^-?[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?$'
)

SELECT
    line_item_id,
    staging_amount_text,
    staging_amount_text::numeric AS staging_amount,
    mart_amount,
    ABS(staging_amount_text::numeric - COALESCE(mart_amount, 0)) AS abs_diff,
    ref_no,
    item,
    vendor,
    date
FROM matched
WHERE ABS(staging_amount_text::numeric - COALESCE(mart_amount, 0)) > 0.01

test.mpi_analytics.assert_no_missing_row.raw_code:
{{ config(tags=['reconciliation']) }}

/*
Test: No Missing Rows in Map Mart
Description: Verifies that mart__invoice_items_map contains all rows from
             mart__invoice_items that pass the map mart's is_active filter
             (WHERE is_active = TRUE OR is_active IS NULL).

Expected Result: 0 rows (test passes)
Failure Condition: Rows in mart__invoice_items that should appear in
                   mart__invoice_items_map based on the is_active filter,
                   but are absent.

Defined in: mart__invoice_items_map (final WHERE clause).
Both marts read from int__invoice_items_with_normalized_fields, but they differ:
  - mart__invoice_items: selects all rows (no is_active filter)
  - mart__invoice_items_map: applies WHERE is_active = TRUE OR is_active IS NULL
Rows with is_active = FALSE legitimately exist in the main mart but not the map
mart. Since the main mart doesn't carry is_active as a column, we join to the
intermediate model to check the filter. Only active/null rows are expected to
appear in both marts.
*/

SELECT
    mart.invoice_items_id,
    mart.item,
    mart.vendor,
    mart.ref_no,
    mart.date
FROM {{ ref('mart__invoice_items') }} mart
INNER JOIN {{ ref('int__invoice_items_with_normalized_fields') }} interm
    ON mart.invoice_items_id = interm.invoice_items_id
LEFT JOIN {{ ref('mart__invoice_items_map') }} map_mart
    ON mart.invoice_items_id = map_mart.id
WHERE map_mart.id IS NULL
  AND (interm.is_active = TRUE OR interm.is_active IS NULL)

{{ config(tags=['reconciliation']) }}

/*
Test: No Unexplained Extra Rows in Mart
Description: Starts from mart__invoice_items, LEFT JOINs back to staging line items.
             Rows in the mart that have no corresponding staging line item are categorized
             as known synthetic records (tax, freight, misc charges) or unexplained.
             Fails only on truly unexplained extra rows.

Expected Result: 0 rows (test passes)
Failure Condition: Mart rows that cannot be traced back to any staging line item
                   and are not a known synthetic record type.

Known synthetic categories (not failures):
  - synthetic_tax: tax line added from global fields
  - synthetic_freight: freight line added from global fields
  - synthetic_misc: misc charge from global fields misc_charges_raw JSONB

Why mart rows can exist without a staging source:
  int__extracted_data_combined creates synthetic records by UNION ALL'ing
  tax, freight, and misc charge rows onto the real line items from
  stg__extracted_line_items. These synthetic rows get deterministic IDs
  (HASHTEXTEXTENDED) that won't match any staging line_item_id, so they
  appear as "extra" in this reconciliation.

  We identify them by recomputing the same deterministic hash from
  stg__extracted_global_fields, matching the exact ID generation logic
  in int__extracted_data_combined. This avoids heuristic-based matching
  (e.g. checking description text) which could mask real issues.
*/

/*
  Defined in: int__extracted_data_combined (tax_records CTE).
  Tax IDs are: ABS(HASHTEXTEXTENDED(extraction_invoice_id || '-tax', 0))
*/
WITH synthetic_tax_ids AS (
    SELECT ABS(HASHTEXTEXTENDED(extraction_invoice_id::text || '-tax', 0)) AS synthetic_id
    FROM {{ ref('stg__extracted_global_fields') }}
),

/*
  Defined in: int__extracted_data_combined (freight_records CTE).
  Freight IDs are: ABS(HASHTEXTEXTENDED(extraction_invoice_id || '-freight', 0))
*/
synthetic_freight_ids AS (
    SELECT ABS(HASHTEXTEXTENDED(extraction_invoice_id::text || '-freight', 0)) AS synthetic_id
    FROM {{ ref('stg__extracted_global_fields') }}
),

/*
  Defined in: int__extracted_data_combined (misc_charges_records CTE).
  Misc IDs are: ABS(HASHTEXTEXTENDED(extraction_invoice_id || '-misc-' || ordinality, 0))
  One ID per entry in the misc_charges_raw JSONB array.
*/
synthetic_misc_ids AS (
    SELECT ABS(HASHTEXTEXTENDED(g.extraction_invoice_id::text || '-misc-' || mc_order::text, 0)) AS synthetic_id
    FROM {{ ref('stg__extracted_global_fields') }} g,
    LATERAL jsonb_array_elements(g.misc_charges_raw) WITH ORDINALITY AS mc(charge, mc_order)
    WHERE g.misc_charges_raw IS NOT NULL AND jsonb_array_length(g.misc_charges_raw) > 0
),

mart_rows AS (
    SELECT
        mart.invoice_items_id,
        mart.item,
        mart.description,
        mart.vendor,
        mart.ref_no,
        mart.date,
        mart.amount
    FROM {{ ref('mart__invoice_items') }} mart
),

/*
  Join mart back to staging by invoice_items_id = line_item_id.
  Rows where staging_id IS NULL have no staging source.
*/
with_staging AS (
    SELECT
        m.*,
        li.line_item_id AS staging_id
    FROM mart_rows m
    LEFT JOIN {{ ref('stg__extracted_line_items') }} li
        ON m.invoice_items_id = li.line_item_id
),

unmatched AS (
    SELECT
        w.*,
        CASE
            WHEN w.invoice_items_id IN (SELECT synthetic_id FROM synthetic_tax_ids)
                THEN 'synthetic_tax'
            WHEN w.invoice_items_id IN (SELECT synthetic_id FROM synthetic_freight_ids)
                THEN 'synthetic_freight'
            WHEN w.invoice_items_id IN (SELECT synthetic_id FROM synthetic_misc_ids)
                THEN 'synthetic_misc'
            ELSE 'UNEXPLAINED'
        END AS extra_reason
    FROM with_staging w
    WHERE w.staging_id IS NULL
)

SELECT
    invoice_items_id,
    item,
    description,
    vendor,
    ref_no,
    date,
    amount,
    extra_reason
FROM unmatched
WHERE extra_reason = 'UNEXPLAINED'

test.mpi_analytics.assert_no_unexplained.name: assert_no_unexplained_missing_rows_in_mart
test.mpi_analytics.assert_no_unexplained.raw_code:
{{ config(tags=['reconciliation']) }}

/*
Test: No Unexplained Missing Rows in Mart
Description: Starts from staging sources (stg__extracted_line_items + stg__extracted_global_fields),
             LEFT JOINs to mart__invoice_items. For rows missing from the mart, categorizes them
             by the known business filter that explains the exclusion.
             Fails only on rows that are missing for no known reason.

Expected Result: 0 rows (test passes)
Failure Condition: Staging rows that should have reached the mart but didn't.

Known exclusion categories (not failures):
  - filtered_by_validation: validation_score <= threshold AND status != 'model_approved'
  - filtered_empty_item: item is NULL or empty
  - filtered_bad_description: description starts with "INVOICE", is date-like, or is "?"
  - filtered_empty_ref_no: ref_no is NULL or blank (entire PDF rejected)
  - filtered_dedup: superseded by a newer extraction of the same logical invoice
  - filtered_email_status: email queue record not in DOWNLOADED status
  - filtered_ys_date_cutoff: Y & S Plumbing Supply before 2018-04-22
  - filtered_item_cleaning: non-product items (Header, Customer Discount) or legacy codes
*/

/*
  Line items only have item-level data (item, description, qty, cost, amount).
  Global fields (ref_no, vendor, date, status, validation_score, email_queue_id)
  live on the invoice level in stg__extracted_global_fields. We need both to
  evaluate the business filters that happen downstream.
*/
WITH staging AS (
    SELECT
        li.line_item_id AS invoice_items_id,
        li.extraction_id,
        li.extraction_invoice_id,
        li.s3_file_key AS filename,
        li.item,
        li.description,
        li.amount,
        li.extracted_at,
        g.ref_no,
        g.vendor,
        g.date,
        g.status,
        g.validation_score,
        g.email_queue_id
    FROM {{ ref('stg__extracted_line_items') }} li
    INNER JOIN {{ ref('stg__extracted_global_fields') }} g
        ON li.extraction_invoice_id = g.extraction_invoice_id
),

/*
  Every staging row should have a matching mart row via line_item_id = invoice_items_id
  (deterministic hash set in int__extracted_data_combined).
  Rows that don't match are "missing from mart" and need to be explained.
*/
missing_from_mart AS (
    SELECT stg.*
    FROM staging stg
    LEFT JOIN {{ ref('mart__invoice_items') }} mart
        ON stg.invoice_items_id = mart.invoice_items_id
    WHERE mart.invoice_items_id IS NULL
),

/* Email metadata for checking email_status and sender/subject filters. */
email_status_lookup AS (
    SELECT id, status AS email_status, sender, subject
    FROM {{ ref('stg__email_download_queue') }}
),

/*
  Defined in: int__extracted_data_combined_compat (filename_ref_no_validation CTE).
  If ANY line item in a PDF file has an empty ref_no, the ENTIRE file is rejected
  (filename_has_valid_ref_no = FALSE). We replicate this by collecting all filenames
  where any staging row has a blank ref_no.
*/
filenames_with_empty_ref_no AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT s.filename
    FROM staging s
    WHERE s.ref_no IS NULL
       OR TRIM(s.ref_no) = ''
       OR TRIM(s.ref_no) ~ '^[\s]*$'
),

/*
  Defined in: int__extracted_data_combined_compat (latest_only CTE).
  The compat layer deduplicates by DENSE_RANK over (vendor, patched_ref_no, date),
  keeping only the "best" extraction (ordered by email_date, validation_score,
  status, extraction_id). Rows from losing extractions are dropped.

  We detect dedup losers by checking: does the mart already have rows for the
  same ref_no + date from a DIFFERENT extraction? If yes, this staging row
  lost the dedup race. We use mart.invoice_id (which equals extraction_id from
  the compat layer) instead of re-joining to staging, because the staging
  post-hook may delete old extractions. The regexp_replace mirrors the
  1- → I- ref_no patch applied in the compat layer.

  Note: The compat dedup key also includes vendor, but we can't reliably match
  on vendor here because the mart stores the resolved vendor (email-derived)
  while staging has the raw OCR vendor — they differ in spelling/casing.
  The risk of a false positive (different vendor, same ref_no + date) is low
  since invoice numbers are vendor-specific.
*/
dedup_losers AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT m.invoice_items_id
    FROM missing_from_mart m
    WHERE EXISTS (
        SELECT 1
        FROM {{ ref('mart__invoice_items') }} mart
        WHERE mart.invoice_id != m.extraction_id
          AND (
              mart.ref_no = m.ref_no
              OR mart.ref_no = regexp_replace(m.ref_no, '^1-', 'I-')
          )
          AND mart.date = m.date
    )
),

categorized AS (
    SELECT
        m.*,
        CASE
            /*
              Defined in: int__extracted_data_combined_compat (WHERE clause).
              Only rows with status='model_approved' OR validation_score > threshold survive.
            */
            WHEN m.status != 'model_approved'
                 AND (m.validation_score IS NULL OR m.validation_score <= {{ var('min_validation_score') }})
                THEN 'filtered_by_validation'

            /*
              Defined in: int__extracted_data_combined_compat (WHERE clause).
              Rows with empty or NULL item are excluded.
            */
            WHEN m.item IS NULL OR TRIM(m.item) = ''
                THEN 'filtered_empty_item'

            /*
              Defined in: int__extracted_data_combined_compat (WHERE clause).
              Descriptions starting with "INVOICE" are filtered out.
            */
            WHEN m.description IS NOT NULL AND UPPER(TRIM(m.description)) LIKE 'INVOICE%'
                THEN 'filtered_bad_description'

            /*
              Defined in: int__extracted_data_combined_compat (WHERE clause).
              Date-like descriptions (e.g. "01/15/2024") are filtered out.
            */
            WHEN m.description IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(m.description) ~ '^\d{1,2}/\d{1,2}/\d{2,4}(\s|$)'
                THEN 'filtered_date_description'

            /*
              Defined in: int__extracted_data_combined_compat (WHERE clause).
              Descriptions that are just "?" are filtered out.
            */
            WHEN m.description IS NOT NULL AND TRIM(m.description) = '?'
                THEN 'filtered_question_description'

            /*
              Defined in: int__extracted_data_combined_compat (filename_ref_no_validation CTE).
              If any line in the same PDF has empty ref_no, all lines in that file are rejected.
            */
            WHEN m.filename IN (SELECT filename FROM filenames_with_empty_ref_no)
                THEN 'filtered_empty_ref_no'

            /*
              Defined in: int__extracted_data_combined_compat (JOIN to email queue).
              Only emails with status='DOWNLOADED' (or no email record) pass through.
            */
            WHEN es.email_status IS NOT NULL AND es.email_status != 'DOWNLOADED'
                THEN 'filtered_email_status'

            /*
              Defined in: int__extracted_data_combined_compat (WHERE clause).
              Y & S Plumbing Supply invoices on or before 2018-04-22 are excluded because
              the LLM fails to extract item/description properly for older invoices.
              We use LIKE because staging has the OCR vendor name ('Y & S Plumbing Supplies')
              while compat uses the email-derived name ('Y & S PLUMBING SUPPLY').
            */
            WHEN UPPER(TRIM(m.vendor)) LIKE 'Y & S PLUMBING SUPPL%' AND m.date <= '2018-04-22'
                THEN 'filtered_ys_date_cutoff'

            /*
              Defined in: int__extracted_data_items_cleaned (rule_3_exclude_non_products CTE).
              Non-product line items like "Header" (contact info) and "Customer Discount"
              are excluded from the pipeline.
            */
            WHEN UPPER(TRIM(m.item)) IN ('HEADER', 'CUSTOMER DISCOUNT')
                THEN 'filtered_item_cleaning'

            /*
              Defined in: int__extracted_data_items_cleaned (final WHERE clause).
              Two specific legacy item codes are hardcoded for exclusion.
            */
            WHEN m.item IN ('SP*00001075', 'SP*00001076')
                THEN 'filtered_legacy_item'

            /*
              Defined in: int__extracted_data_combined_compat (latest_only CTE).
              This row's extraction lost the dedup race — another extraction for the same
              invoice (same ref_no + date) produced the rows that appear in the mart.
            */
            WHEN m.invoice_items_id IN (SELECT invoice_items_id FROM dedup_losers)
                THEN 'filtered_dedup'

            ELSE 'UNEXPLAINED'
        END AS exclusion_reason
    FROM missing_from_mart m
    LEFT JOIN email_status_lookup es ON m.email_queue_id = es.id
)

SELECT
    invoice_items_id,
    filename,
    item,
    description,
    ref_no,
    vendor,
    date,
    status,
    validation_score,
    exclusion_reason
FROM categorized
WHERE exclusion_reason = 'UNEXPLAINED'

            WHEN m.invoice_items_id IN (SELECT invoice_items_id FROM dedup_losers)
                THEN 'filtered_dedup'

            ELSE 'UNEXPLAINED'
        END AS exclusion_reason
    FROM missing_from_mart m
    LEFT JOIN email_status_lookup es ON m.email_queue_id = es.id
)

    filename,
    item,
    description,
    ref_no,
    vendor,
    date,
    status,
    validation_score,
    exclusion_reason
FROM categorized
WHERE exclusion_reason = 'UNEXPLAINED'

test.mpi_analytics.assert_row_count_reco.raw_code:
{{ config(tags=['reconciliation']) }}

/*
Test: Row Count Reconciliation
Description: Compares staging row count to mart row count, breaking down the difference
             into staging rows that matched the mart, mart rows not in staging (synthetic),
             and any unexplained difference. Fails if the numbers don't balance.

Expected Result: 0 rows (test passes)
Failure Condition: mart_rows - staging_rows_in_mart - mart_synthetic_rows != 0,
                   meaning there are rows in the mart that can't be accounted for by
                   either staging line items or known synthetic records.

Why the counts differ:
  - Staging has MORE rows than mart because business filters in the pipeline
    (validation, dedup, item cleaning, etc.) drop rows before the mart.
  - Mart has EXTRA rows not in staging because int__extracted_data_combined
    synthesizes tax, freight, and misc charge records from invoice-level totals.
  - The equation: mart = staging_matched + synthetic. If it doesn't balance,
    something is creating or losing rows unexpectedly.
*/

/*
  Total staging rows: join line items to global fields (same join used by the
  pipeline in int__extracted_data_combined) to count only rows that have
  a valid global fields parent.
*/
WITH staging_count AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM {{ ref('stg__extracted_line_items') }} li
    INNER JOIN {{ ref('stg__extracted_global_fields') }} g
        ON li.extraction_invoice_id = g.extraction_invoice_id
),

mart_count AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM {{ ref('mart__invoice_items') }}
),

/*
  Staging rows that made it to the mart (matched by line_item_id = invoice_items_id).
  These survived all business filters and appear in the final table.
*/
staging_in_mart AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM {{ ref('stg__extracted_line_items') }} li
    INNER JOIN {{ ref('mart__invoice_items') }} mart
        ON li.line_item_id = mart.invoice_items_id
),

/*
  Mart rows with no staging source — these are the synthetic records
  (tax, freight, misc) created by int__extracted_data_combined.
*/
mart_not_in_staging AS (
    SELECT COUNT(*) AS cnt
    FROM {{ ref('mart__invoice_items') }} mart
    LEFT JOIN {{ ref('stg__extracted_line_items') }} li
        ON mart.invoice_items_id = li.line_item_id
    WHERE li.line_item_id IS NULL
)

SELECT
    s.cnt AS staging_rows,
    m.cnt AS mart_rows,
    sim.cnt AS staging_rows_in_mart,
    mns.cnt AS mart_rows_not_in_staging,
    s.cnt - sim.cnt AS staging_rows_filtered_out,
    m.cnt - sim.cnt - mns.cnt AS unexplained_diff
FROM staging_count s, mart_count m, staging_in_mart sim, mart_not_in_staging mns
WHERE m.cnt - sim.cnt - mns.cnt != 0

test.mpi_analytics.test_duplicate_ref_no.name: test_duplicate_ref_no_validation
test.mpi_analytics.test_duplicate_ref_no.raw_code:
{{
  config(
    severity = 'warn',
    warn_if = '>0'
  )
}}
/*
Test: Reference Number Business Rules Validation
Description: Validates ref_no distribution across vendors in mart__invoice_items.
             Reports suspicious patterns but allows legitimate business cases.

Purpose: Monitor ref_no usage patterns and identify potential data quality issues
         while respecting business rule that same ref_no can legitimately appear
         across different suppliers or dates.

Expected Result: 0 rows (test passes)
Failure Condition: Rows returned indicate potential data quality issues to investigate
*/

WITH ref_no_analysis AS (
    SELECT
        ref_no,
        COUNT(*) as total_occurrences,
        COUNT(DISTINCT vendor) as unique_vendors,
        COUNT(DISTINCT date) as unique_dates,
        COUNT(DISTINCT item) as unique_items,
        STRING_AGG(DISTINCT vendor, ', ') as vendors_list,
        STRING_AGG(DISTINCT date::text, ', ') as dates_list
    FROM {{ ref('mart__invoice_items') }}
    WHERE ref_no IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY ref_no
),

suspicious_patterns AS (
    SELECT
        ref_no,
        total_occurrences,
        unique_vendors,
        unique_dates,
        unique_items,
        vendors_list,
        dates_list,
        CASE
            -- Same ref_no, same vendor, same date, but many different items (>10)
            WHEN unique_vendors = 1 AND unique_dates = 1 AND unique_items > 10
            THEN 'LARGE_INVOICE: ' || ref_no || ' has ' || unique_items || ' items from same vendor/date'

            -- Same ref_no used by >5 different vendors (unlikely but possible)
            WHEN unique_vendors > 5
            THEN 'MULTI_VENDOR_SUSPICIOUS: ' || ref_no || ' used by ' || unique_vendors || ' vendors'

            -- For debugging: cases where ref_no appears >50 times total
            WHEN total_occurrences > 50
            THEN 'HIGH_FREQUENCY: ' || ref_no || ' appears ' || total_occurrences || ' times'

            ELSE NULL
        END as warning_message
    FROM ref_no_analysis
)

SELECT
    ref_no,
    total_occurrences,
    unique_vendors,
    unique_dates,
    unique_items,
    vendors_list,
    dates_list,
    warning_message
FROM suspicious_patterns
WHERE warning_message IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY total_occurrences DESC, unique_vendors DESC

test.mpi_analytics.assert_extraction_inv.raw_code:
/*
Test: Extraction Invoice ID Referential Integrity
Description: Validates that every extraction_invoice_id in stg__extracted_line_items
             has a corresponding row in stg__extracted_global_fields.
             This is an orphan check for multi-invoice PDF extraction where each PDF
             may produce multiple invoices, each identified by extraction_invoice_id
             (a deterministic hash of extraction_id + invoice_index).

Purpose: Ensure referential integrity between line items and global fields after
         multi-invoice PDF extraction. Orphan line items indicate a mismatch in
         how invoices are unnested between the two staging models.

Expected Result: 0 rows (test passes)
Failure Condition: Any rows returned indicate line items referencing an
                   extraction_invoice_id that does not exist in global fields.
*/

SELECT
    li.extraction_invoice_id,
    li.extraction_id,
    li.invoice_index,
    li.s3_file_key,
    COUNT(*) AS orphan_line_item_count
FROM {{ ref('stg__extracted_line_items') }} li
LEFT JOIN {{ ref('stg__extracted_global_fields') }} gf
    ON li.extraction_invoice_id = gf.extraction_invoice_id
WHERE gf.extraction_invoice_id IS NULL
GROUP BY
    li.extraction_invoice_id,
    li.extraction_id,
    li.invoice_index,
    li.s3_file_key
ORDER BY orphan_line_item_count DESC

test.mpi_analytics.test_email_vendor_map.raw_code:
/*
Test: Email-Based Vendor Mapping Validation
Description: Validates vendor mapping completeness and exclusions in stg__model_extracted_data.
             Ensures vendor information is properly derived from email senders for DOWNLOADED status records.

Purpose: Monitor email-to-vendor mapping coverage and ensure excluded vendors are properly filtered out.

Expected Result: 0 rows (test passes)
Failure Condition: >10% unmapped vendors OR any excluded vendors present (Positive Tech, MPI Plumbing Corp)
*/

WITH vendor_stats AS (
    SELECT
        COUNT(*) as total_records,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN vendor IS NULL THEN 1 END) as unmapped_count,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN vendor = 'Positive Tech' OR vendor = 'MPI Plumbing Corp' THEN 1 END) as excluded_count,
        COUNT(CASE WHEN vendor IS NOT NULL THEN 1 END) as mapped_count
    FROM {{ ref('int__model_extracted_data') }}
),

detailed_analysis AS (
    SELECT
        total_records,
        unmapped_count,
        excluded_count,
        mapped_count,
        ROUND(unmapped_count * 100.0 / NULLIF(total_records, 0), 2) as unmapped_percentage,
        CASE
            WHEN unmapped_count * 100.0 / NULLIF(total_records, 0) > 10.0
            THEN 'UNMAPPED_THRESHOLD_EXCEEDED: ' || ROUND(unmapped_count * 100.0 / NULLIF(total_records, 0), 2) || '% unmapped (>10% threshold)'
            WHEN excluded_count > 0
            THEN 'EXCLUDED_VENDORS_PRESENT: ' || excluded_count || ' records with excluded vendors (Positive Tech, MPI Plumbing Corp)'
            ELSE NULL
        END as failure_reason
    FROM vendor_stats
)

-- Return results only when test should fail
SELECT
    total_records,
    mapped_count,
    unmapped_count,
    excluded_count,
    unmapped_percentage,
    failure_reason
FROM detailed_analysis
WHERE failure_reason IS NOT NULL

test.mpi_analytics.test_intermediate_dup.name: test_intermediate_duplicate_ref_no
test.mpi_analytics.test_intermediate_dup.raw_code:
{{
  config(
    severity = 'warn',
    warn_if = '>0'
  )
}}
/*
Test: Intermediate Layer Window Function Validation
Description: Validates that the latest_only window function is working correctly.
             Only checks for true duplicates (same vendor, ref_no, date, item appearing multiple times).

Purpose: Ensure window function deduplication works as intended.
         Different suppliers using same ref_no is EXPECTED and not an error.

Expected Result: 0 rows (test passes)
Failure Condition: Any rows returned (window function failed to deduplicate properly)
*/

WITH true_duplicates AS (
    SELECT
        ref_no,
        vendor,
        date,
        item,
        COUNT(*) as occurrence_count,
        STRING_AGG(
            'ID: ' || invoice_items_id ||
            ' | Date Added: ' || COALESCE(date_added::text, 'NULL') ||
            ' | Invoice ID: ' || COALESCE(invoice_id::text, 'NULL'),
            ' || '
            ORDER BY date_added DESC, invoice_items_id DESC
        ) as duplicate_details
    FROM {{ ref('int__model_extracted_data') }}
    WHERE ref_no IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY ref_no, vendor, date, item
    HAVING COUNT(*) > 1
)

-- Only flag true duplicates (same business key appearing multiple times)
SELECT
    ref_no,
    vendor,
    date,
    item,
    occurrence_count,
    'WINDOW_FUNCTION_FAILURE: Same (vendor, ref_no, date, item) appears ' ||
    occurrence_count || ' times. Details: ' || duplicate_details as error_message
FROM true_duplicates
ORDER BY occurrence_count DESC, ref_no

macro.mpi_analytics.resolve_temp_mpi_ite.name: resolve_temp_mpi_item
macro.mpi_analytics.resolve_temp_mpi_ite.macro_sql:
{% macro resolve_temp_mpi_item(sheet_name_column) %}
{#
    Resolves the MPI item code for temporary mappings based on sheet name.

    Maps sheet names to account types using the sheet_account_mapping seed table:
    - E (Equipment sheets) -> 'UIDI - Job Equipment'
    - M (Materials sheets) -> 'UIDI - Job Materials Purchased'
    - Other/Unknown -> 'UIDI-' || sheet_name (fallback)

    Normalizes sheet names by:
    - Replacing ") (" with " - "
    - Removing remaining parentheses
    - Converting to uppercase

    The mapping is maintained in seeds/sheet_account_mapping.csv for easy updates.

    Usage:
        {{ resolve_temp_mpi_item('temp_sheet_name') }}
#}
COALESCE(
    (
        SELECT mpi_item_template
        FROM {{ ref('sheet_account_mapping') }}
        WHERE sheet_name = UPPER({{ normalize_sheet_name(sheet_name_column) }})
    ),
    'UIDI-' || COALESCE({{ sheet_name_column }}, 'UNKNOWN')
)
{% endmacro %}

macro.mpi_analytics.normalize_address.name: normalize_address
macro.mpi_analytics.normalize_address.description:
Normalizes address formatting by applying title case and normalizing street type abbreviations.

This macro ensures consistent address formatting across all records by:
1. Converting the address to title case (e.g., "MAIN STREET" -> "Main Street")
2. Normalizing street type abbreviations:
   - "Street" -> "St."
   - "Avenue" -> "Ave."
   - "Road" -> "Rd."
3. Fixing incorrect punctuation (e.g., "St," -> "St.")
4. Fixing typos (e.g., Hilside -> Hillside)

arguments.name: address_column
arguments.description: The name of the address column to normalize (e.g., 'customer_job')

macro.mpi_analytics.normalize_sheet_name.name: normalize_sheet_name
macro.mpi_analytics.normalize_sheet_name.macro_sql:
{% macro normalize_sheet_name(sheet_name_column) %}
{#
    Normalizes sheet name format by removing parentheses and periods,
    replacing ") (" patterns with dash for consistency.

    Normalization steps:
    1. Replace ") (" with " - " (converts "(BLACK MALLEABLE) (GAS)" to "BLACK MALLEABLE - GAS")
    2. Remove remaining parentheses
    3. Remove periods
    4. Collapse multiple spaces to single space and trim
    5. Handle NULL/empty values by returning 'NO SHEET NAME'

    Examples:
      - "(AIR FITTINGS)" -> "AIR FITTINGS"
      - "(BLACK MALLEABLE) (GAS)" -> "BLACK MALLEABLE - GAS"
      - NULL or "" -> "NO SHEET NAME"

    Usage:
        {{ normalize_sheet_name('m.resolved_sheet_name') }}
        {{ normalize_sheet_name('temp_sheet_name') }}
#}
CASE
    WHEN {{ sheet_name_column }} IS NULL OR TRIM({{ sheet_name_column }}) = ''
    THEN 'NO SHEET NAME'
    ELSE TRIM(
        REGEXP_REPLACE(
            REGEXP_REPLACE(
                REGEXP_REPLACE(
                    REGEXP_REPLACE({{ sheet_name_column }}, '\)\s*\(', ' - ', 'g'),
                    '[()]', '', 'g'
                ),
                '\.', '', 'g'
            ),
            '\s+', ' ', 'g'
        )
    )
END
{% endmacro %}
macro.mpi_analytics.normalize_sheet_name.description:
Normalizes sheet name formatting by removing parentheses and periods,
and standardizing multi-part sheet names with dashes.

This macro ensures consistent sheet name formatting across all records by:
1. Replacing ") (" with " - " to convert multi-part sheet names
2. Removing all remaining parentheses
3. Removing all periods
4. Collapsing multiple spaces to single space
5. Trimming leading/trailing whitespace
6. Replacing NULL or empty values with 'NO SHEET NAME'

**Examples:**
  - Input: "(AIR FITTINGS)"
    Output: "AIR FITTINGS"

  - Input: "(BLACK MALLEABLE) (GAS)"
    Output: "BLACK MALLEABLE - GAS"

  - Input: NULL or ""
    Output: "NO SHEET NAME"

arguments.name: sheet_name_column
arguments.description:
The name of the sheet_name column to normalize.
Can include table aliases (e.g., 'm.resolved_sheet_name', 'temp_sheet_name')

macro.mpi_analytics.create_normalize_buy.description:
Creates the PostgreSQL function normalize_buyer_fn that performs buyer name normalization.
This function should be called during dbt initialization to ensure the function exists in the database.

The function is IMMUTABLE, meaning it always returns the same result for the same input,
which allows PostgreSQL to optimize queries that use it.

macro.mpi_analytics.normalize_buyer.name: normalize_buyer
macro.mpi_analytics.normalize_buyer.description:
Normalizes buyer names to a consistent format by:
1. Removing all non-alphanumeric characters (including spaces)
2. Separating alphabetic and numeric segments
3. Formatting as Title Case "Alphabetic Numeric" (first letter uppercase, rest lowercase)
4. Adding space separator between alphabetic and numeric parts if both exist

This macro creates a PostgreSQL function normalize_buyer_fn that performs the normalization.
The function is marked as IMMUTABLE for query optimization.

Examples:
  - "AR LE M 9 29 44 2 -9 55 8" becomes "Arlem 9294429558"
  - "ARLEM 929 442-9558" becomes "Arlem 9294429558"
  - "Arlem(929) 442-955" becomes "Arlem 929442955"
  - "Modachi Dutech" becomes "Modachidutech" (spaces removed)
  - "ANTHONY" becomes "Anthony"
  - "DAVIDW 3478048772" becomes "Davidw 3478048772"
  - "( 8 62 ) 3 18 - 00 7 4" becomes "8623180074"
  
Usage: normalize_buyer_fn(buyer_column)
  
Returns:
  - Normalized buyer name string in Title Case format
  - NULL if input is NULL
  - Empty string if input is empty or contains no alphanumeric characters

arguments.name: buyer_column
arguments.description: The column containing the buyer name to normalize

macro.mpi_analytics.map_from_lists.name: map_from_lists
macro.mpi_analytics.map_from_lists.description:
Map "bad" values to "good" values. Where the "bad" values is a list of examples and the "good" values
are the keys in the map.

It takes a column name and a map (a dictionary where keys are desired "good" values and values are
lists of "bad" or inconsistent values). The macro generates a SQL CASE statement that transforms
values in the specified column: if a value in the column matches any of the "bad" values
(case-insensitive), it is replaced with the corresponding "good" value from the map; otherwise,
the original column value is retained.

arguments.name: column_name
arguments.description: The name of the column to get values from

macro.mpi_analytics.safe_cast.name: safe_cast
macro.mpi_analytics.safe_cast.macro_sql:
{% macro safe_cast(field_to_cast, type_to_cast_to) %}

    {% set clean_field = "REPLACE(" ~ field_to_cast ~ ", ',', '')" %}

    CASE
        -- Check if the field is not null, not empty, has reasonable length, and matches numeric pattern
        -- This replicates the logic from InvoiceItems._safe_numeric_cast in Python:
        -- - Removes commas
        -- - Validates with a regex so bad rows don't crash the query
        -- - Returns NULL when non-numeric so comparisons behave as expected
        -- - Limits length to prevent extremely long strings from causing issues
        WHEN {{ field_to_cast }} IS NOT NULL
            AND {{ field_to_cast }} != ''
            AND LENGTH({{ field_to_cast }}) < 100
            AND {{ clean_field }} ~ '^-?[0-9]*\.?[0-9]+$'
        THEN
            -- Cast to target type
            ({{ clean_field }}::{{ type_to_cast_to }})
        ELSE
            -- Return NULL for invalid values
            NULL
    END

{% endmacro %}
macro.mpi_analytics.safe_cast.description:
Safely casts a text field to a numeric type, returning NULL if the value is not numeric.
This prevents SQL errors when casting invalid values and handles comma-separated numbers.

The macro removes commas from the field value, checks if it matches a numeric pattern
(including negative and decimal numbers), and casts to the target type if valid.

arguments.name: field_to_cast
arguments.description: The name of the field to cast (e.g., 'amount', 'cost', 'qty')

macro.mpi_analytics.add_vendor_suffix.name: add_vendor_suffix
macro.mpi_analytics.add_vendor_suffix.macro_sql:
{% macro add_vendor_suffix(item_column, vendor_column) %}
    -- Add suffix based on vendor name matching
    CASE
        -- Match vendor name patterns (case-insensitive, ordered by specificity)
        WHEN UPPER({{ vendor_column }}) LIKE '%BMW%' THEN {{item_column}} || '-B'
        WHEN UPPER({{ vendor_column }}) LIKE '%WORLD WIDE%' OR UPPER({{ vendor_column }}) LIKE '%WWPS%' THEN {{item_column}} || '-W'
        WHEN UPPER({{ vendor_column }}) LIKE '%Y & S%' OR UPPER({{ vendor_column }}) LIKE '%Y&S%' THEN {{item_column}} || '-Y'
        WHEN UPPER({{ vendor_column }}) LIKE '%SUPREME%' THEN {{item_column}} || '-S'
        WHEN UPPER({{ vendor_column }}) LIKE '%PYRAMID%' THEN {{item_column}} || '-P'
        WHEN UPPER({{ vendor_column }}) LIKE '%PARK%' AND UPPER({{ vendor_column }}) NOT LIKE '%CENTRAL PARK%' THEN {{item_column}} || '-PA'
        WHEN UPPER({{ vendor_column }}) LIKE '%GOTHAM%' THEN {{item_column}} || '-G'
        WHEN UPPER({{ vendor_column }}) LIKE '%FW WEBB%' OR UPPER({{ vendor_column }}) LIKE '%F.W. WEBB%' THEN {{item_column}} || '-F'
        WHEN UPPER({{ vendor_column }}) LIKE '%FLOW MARK%' OR UPPER({{ vendor_column }}) LIKE '%FLOWMARK%' THEN {{item_column}} || '-F'
        WHEN UPPER({{ vendor_column }}) LIKE '%ABC OPUS%' THEN {{item_column}} || '-A'
        WHEN UPPER({{ vendor_column }}) LIKE '%AF SUPPLY%' THEN {{item_column}} || '-A'
        WHEN UPPER({{ vendor_column }}) LIKE '%BRUCE%' THEN {{item_column}} || '-BR'
        WHEN UPPER({{ vendor_column }}) LIKE '%PLUMBING EXCHANGE%' THEN {{item_column}} || '-PE'
        -- No suffix for unrecognized vendors, return the same values
        ELSE {{item_column}}
    END
{% endmacro %}
macro.mpi_analytics.add_vendor_suffix.description:
Add vendor-specific suffix to item codes based on vendor name.

Replicates Python's InvoiceItems._add_suffix_to_item() logic.
Essential for model_extracted_data items to match legacy invoice_items.

Administrative Items (No Suffix):
- Tax, freight, shipping, handling, subtotal, total
- "10 Materials", "11 Equipment" (category headers)
- NULL or empty items

Suffix Mapping:
- B = BMW, W = World Wide/WWPS, Y = Y&S
- S = Supreme, P = Park/Pyramid, G = Gotham
- F = Flow Mark/FW Webb, A = ABC Opus/AF Supply

Cleaning Logic:
- Removes existing suffixes before adding new one
- Prevents double-suffix issues (e.g., "88958-B-B")

macro.dbt_postgres.postgres__get_relatio.name: postgres__get_relations
macro.dbt_postgres.postgres__get_relatio.macro_sql:
{% macro postgres__get_relations() -%}

  {#
      -- in pg_depend, objid is the dependent, refobjid is the referenced object
      --  > a pg_depend entry indicates that the referenced object cannot be
      --  > dropped without also dropping the dependent object.
  #}

  {%- call statement('relations', fetch_result=True) -%}
    with relation as (
        select
            pg_rewrite.ev_class as class,
            pg_rewrite.oid as id
        from pg_rewrite
    ),
    class as (
        select
            oid as id,
            relname as name,
            relnamespace as schema,
            relkind as kind
        from pg_class
    ),
    dependency as (
        select distinct
            pg_depend.objid as id,
            pg_depend.refobjid as ref
        from pg_depend
    ),
    schema as (
        select
            pg_namespace.oid as id,
            pg_namespace.nspname as name
        from pg_namespace
        where nspname != 'information_schema' and nspname not like 'pg\_%'
    ),
    referenced as (
        select
            relation.id AS id,
            referenced_class.name ,
            referenced_class.schema ,
            referenced_class.kind
        from relation
        join class as referenced_class on relation.class=referenced_class.id
        where referenced_class.kind in ('r', 'v', 'm')
    ),
    relationships as (
        select
            referenced.name as referenced_name,
            referenced.schema as referenced_schema_id,
            dependent_class.name as dependent_name,
            dependent_class.schema as dependent_schema_id,
            referenced.kind as kind
        from referenced
        join dependency on referenced.id=dependency.id
        join class as dependent_class on dependency.ref=dependent_class.id
        where
            (referenced.name != dependent_class.name or
             referenced.schema != dependent_class.schema)
    )

    select
        referenced_schema.name as referenced_schema,
        relationships.referenced_name as referenced_name,
        dependent_schema.name as dependent_schema,
        relationships.dependent_name as dependent_name
    from relationships
    join schema as dependent_schema on relationships.dependent_schema_id=dependent_schema.id
    join schema as referenced_schema on relationships.referenced_schema_id=referenced_schema.id
    group by referenced_schema, referenced_name, dependent_schema, dependent_name
    order by referenced_schema, referenced_name, dependent_schema, dependent_name;

  {%- endcall -%}

  {{ return(load_result('relations').table) }}
{% endmacro %}

macro.dbt_postgres.postgres__list_relati.macro_sql:
{% macro postgres__list_relations_without_caching(schema_relation) %}
  {% call statement('list_relations_without_caching', fetch_result=True) -%}
    select
      '{{ schema_relation.database }}' as database,
      tablename as name,
      schemaname as schema,
      'table' as type
    from pg_tables
    where schemaname ilike '{{ schema_relation.schema }}'
    union all
    select
      '{{ schema_relation.database }}' as database,
      viewname as name,
      schemaname as schema,
      'view' as type
    from pg_views
    where schemaname ilike '{{ schema_relation.schema }}'
    union all
    select
      '{{ schema_relation.database }}' as database,
      matviewname as name,
      schemaname as schema,
      'materialized_view' as type
    from pg_matviews

macro.dbt_postgres.postgres__get_show_in.macro_sql:
{% macro postgres__get_show_indexes_sql(relation) %}
    select
        i.relname                                   as name,
        m.amname                                    as method,
        ix.indisunique                              as "unique",
        array_to_string(array_agg(a.attname), ',')  as column_names
    from pg_index ix
    join pg_class i
        on i.oid = ix.indexrelid
    join pg_am m
        on m.oid=i.relam
    join pg_class t
        on t.oid = ix.indrelid
    join pg_namespace n
        on n.oid = t.relnamespace
    join pg_attribute a
        on a.attrelid = t.oid
        and a.attnum = ANY(ix.indkey)
    where t.relname = '{{ relation.identifier }}'
      and n.nspname = '{{ relation.schema }}'
      and t.relkind in ('r', 'm')
    group by 1, 2, 3
    order by 1, 2, 3
{% endmacro %}

macro.dbt.default__snapshot_merge_sql.macro_sql:
{% macro default__snapshot_merge_sql(target, source, insert_cols) -%}
    {%- set insert_cols_csv = insert_cols | join(', ') -%}

    merge into {{ target }} as DBT_INTERNAL_DEST
    using {{ source }} as DBT_INTERNAL_SOURCE
    on DBT_INTERNAL_SOURCE.dbt_scd_id = DBT_INTERNAL_DEST.dbt_scd_id

    when matched
     and DBT_INTERNAL_DEST.dbt_valid_to is null
     and DBT_INTERNAL_SOURCE.dbt_change_type in ('update', 'delete')
        then update
        set dbt_valid_to = DBT_INTERNAL_SOURCE.dbt_valid_to

    when not matched
     and DBT_INTERNAL_SOURCE.dbt_change_type = 'insert'
        then insert ({{ insert_cols_csv }})
        values ({{ insert_cols_csv }})

macro.dbt.default__snapshot_staging_tabl.macro_sql:
{% macro default__snapshot_staging_table(strategy, source_sql, target_relation) -%}

    with snapshot_query as (

        {{ source_sql }}

    ),

    snapshotted_data as (

        select *,
            {{ strategy.unique_key }} as dbt_unique_key

        from {{ target_relation }}
        where dbt_valid_to is null

    ),

    insertions_source_data as (

        select
            *,
            {{ strategy.unique_key }} as dbt_unique_key,
            {{ strategy.updated_at }} as dbt_updated_at,
            {{ strategy.updated_at }} as dbt_valid_from,
            nullif({{ strategy.updated_at }}, {{ strategy.updated_at }}) as dbt_valid_to,
            {{ strategy.scd_id }} as dbt_scd_id

        from snapshot_query
    ),

    updates_source_data as (

        select
            *,
            {{ strategy.unique_key }} as dbt_unique_key,
            {{ strategy.updated_at }} as dbt_updated_at,
            {{ strategy.updated_at }} as dbt_valid_from,
            {{ strategy.updated_at }} as dbt_valid_to

        from snapshot_query
    ),

    {%- if strategy.invalidate_hard_deletes %}

    deletes_source_data as (

        select
            *,
            {{ strategy.unique_key }} as dbt_unique_key
        from snapshot_query
    ),
    {% endif %}

    insertions as (

        select
            'insert' as dbt_change_type,
            source_data.*

        from insertions_source_data as source_data
        left outer join snapshotted_data on snapshotted_data.dbt_unique_key = source_data.dbt_unique_key
        where snapshotted_data.dbt_unique_key is null
           or (
                snapshotted_data.dbt_unique_key is not null
            and (
                {{ strategy.row_changed }}
            )
        )

    ),

    updates as (

        select
            'update' as dbt_change_type,
            source_data.*,
            snapshotted_data.dbt_scd_id

        from updates_source_data as source_data
        join snapshotted_data on snapshotted_data.dbt_unique_key = source_data.dbt_unique_key
        where (
            {{ strategy.row_changed }}
        )
    )

    {%- if strategy.invalidate_hard_deletes -%}
    ,

    deletes as (

        select
            'delete' as dbt_change_type,
            source_data.*,
            {{ snapshot_get_time() }} as dbt_valid_from,
            {{ snapshot_get_time() }} as dbt_updated_at,
            {{ snapshot_get_time() }} as dbt_valid_to,
            snapshotted_data.dbt_scd_id

        from snapshotted_data
        left join deletes_source_data as source_data on snapshotted_data.dbt_unique_key = source_data.dbt_unique_key
        where source_data.dbt_unique_key is null
    )
    {%- endif %}

    select * from insertions
    union all
    select * from updates
    {%- if strategy.invalidate_hard_deletes %}
    union all
    select * from deletes
    {%- endif %}

{%- endmacro %}

macro.audit_helper.compare_and_classify_.name: compare_and_classify_query_results
macro.audit_helper.compare_and_classify_.macro_sql:
{% macro compare_and_classify_query_results(a_query, b_query, primary_key_columns=[], columns=[], event_time=None, sample_limit=20) %}
    
    {% set columns = audit_helper._ensure_all_pks_are_in_column_set(primary_key_columns, columns) %}
    {% set joined_cols = columns | join(", ") %}

    {% if event_time %}
        {% set event_time_props = audit_helper._get_comparison_bounds(a_query, b_query, event_time) %}
    {% endif %}

    with 

    {{ audit_helper._generate_set_results(a_query, b_query, primary_key_columns, columns, event_time_props)}}
    
    ,

    all_records as (

        select
            *,
            true as dbt_audit_in_a,
            true as dbt_audit_in_b
        from a_intersect_b

        union all

        select
            *,
            true as dbt_audit_in_a,
            false as dbt_audit_in_b
        from a_except_b

        union all

        select
            *,
            false as dbt_audit_in_a,
            true as dbt_audit_in_b
        from b_except_a

    ),

    classified as (
        select 
            *,
            {{ audit_helper._classify_audit_row_status() }} as dbt_audit_row_status
        from all_records
    ),

    final as (
        select 
            *,
            {{ audit_helper._count_num_rows_in_status() }} as dbt_audit_num_rows_in_status,
            -- using dense_rank so that modified rows (which have a full row for both the left and right side) both get picked up in the sample. 
            -- For every other type this is equivalent to a row_number()
            dense_rank() over (partition by dbt_audit_row_status order by dbt_audit_surrogate_key, dbt_audit_pk_row_num) as dbt_audit_sample_number
        from classified
    )

    select * from final
    {% if sample_limit %}
        where dbt_audit_sample_number <= {{ sample_limit }}
    {% endif %}
    order by dbt_audit_row_status, dbt_audit_sample_number

{% endmacro %}

macro.audit_helper.default__compare_colu.name: default__compare_column_values
macro.audit_helper.default__compare_colu.macro_sql:
{% macro default__compare_column_values(a_query, b_query, primary_key, column_to_compare, emojis, a_relation_name, b_relation_name) -%}
with a_query as (
    {{ a_query }}
),

b_query as (
    {{ b_query }}
),

joined as (
    select
        coalesce(a_query.{{ primary_key }}, b_query.{{ primary_key }}) as {{ primary_key }},
        a_query.{{ column_to_compare }} as a_query_value,
        b_query.{{ column_to_compare }} as b_query_value,
        case
            when a_query.{{ column_to_compare }} = b_query.{{ column_to_compare }} then '{% if emojis %}✅: {% endif %}perfect match'
            when a_query.{{ column_to_compare }} is null and b_query.{{ column_to_compare }} is null then '{% if emojis %}✅: {% endif %}both are null'
            when a_query.{{ primary_key }} is null then '{% if emojis %}🤷: {% endif %}missing from {{ a_relation_name }}'
            when b_query.{{ primary_key }} is null then '{% if emojis %}🤷: {% endif %}missing from {{ b_relation_name }}'
            when a_query.{{ column_to_compare }} is null then '{% if emojis %}🤷: {% endif %}value is null in {{ a_relation_name }} only'
            when b_query.{{ column_to_compare }} is null then '{% if emojis %}🤷: {% endif %}value is null in {{ b_relation_name }} only'
            when a_query.{{ column_to_compare }} != b_query.{{ column_to_compare }} then '{% if emojis %}❌: {% endif %}‍values do not match'
            else 'unknown' -- this should never happen
        end as match_status,
        case
            when a_query.{{ column_to_compare }} = b_query.{{ column_to_compare }} then 0
            when a_query.{{ column_to_compare }} is null and b_query.{{ column_to_compare }} is null then 1
            when a_query.{{ primary_key }} is null then 2
            when b_query.{{ primary_key }} is null then 3
            when a_query.{{ column_to_compare }} is null then 4
            when b_query.{{ column_to_compare }} is null then 5
            when a_query.{{ column_to_compare }} != b_query.{{ column_to_compare }} then 6
            else 7 -- this should never happen
        end as match_order

    from a_query

    full outer join b_query on a_query.{{ primary_key }} = b_query.{{ primary_key }}
),

aggregated as (
    select
        '{{ column_to_compare }}' as column_name,
        match_status,
        match_order,
        count(*) as count_records
    from joined

    group by column_name, match_status, match_order
)

select
    column_name,
    match_status,
    count_records,
    round(100.0 * count_records / sum(count_records) over (), 2) as percent_of_total

from aggregated

order by match_order

{% endmacro %}

            select
                rr.unique_id,
                rr.name as model_name,
                {{ elementary.edr_cast_as_timestamp("rr.execute_completed_at") }}
                as completed_at_utc,
                rr.status
            from {{ run_results_relation }} rr
            cross join sla_deadline sd
            where
                rr.unique_id = '{{ model_unique_id }}'
                and rr.resource_type = 'model'
                and {{ elementary.edr_cast_as_timestamp("rr.execute_completed_at") }}
                >= sd.target_date_start_utc
                and {{ elementary.edr_cast_as_timestamp("rr.execute_completed_at") }}
                <= sd.target_date_end_utc
        ),

        successful_runs as (select * from todays_runs where status = 'success'),

        {# Find runs that completed before the deadline #}
        runs_before_deadline as (
            select sr.*
            from successful_runs sr
            cross join sla_deadline sd
            where sr.completed_at_utc <= sd.deadline_utc
        ),

        sla_result as (
            select
                sd.target_date,
                sd.deadline_utc as sla_deadline_utc,
                (
                    select min(completed_at_utc) from runs_before_deadline
                ) as first_valid_run_utc,
                (
                    select min(completed_at_utc) from successful_runs
                ) as first_successful_run_utc,
                (select count(*) from todays_runs) as total_runs_today,
                (select count(*) from successful_runs) as successful_runs_today,
                case
                    when exists (select 1 from runs_before_deadline)
                    then 'MET_SLA'
                    when exists (select 1 from successful_runs)
                    then 'MISSED_SLA'
                    when exists (select 1 from todays_runs)
                    then 'ALL_FAILED'
                    else 'NOT_RUN'
                end as sla_status
            from sla_deadline sd
        ),

        final_result as (
            select
                '{{ model_name }}' as model_name,
                '{{ model_unique_id }}' as model_unique_id,
                target_date,
                '{{ formatted_sla_time }}' as sla_time,
                '{{ timezone }}' as timezone,
                cast(
                    sla_deadline_utc as {{ elementary.edr_type_string() }}
                ) as sla_deadline_utc,
                sla_status,
                cast(
                    first_valid_run_utc as {{ elementary.edr_type_string() }}
                ) as first_valid_run_utc,
                cast(
                    first_successful_run_utc as {{ elementary.edr_type_string() }}
                ) as first_successful_run_utc,
                total_runs_today,
                successful_runs_today,
                case
                    when sla_status = 'MET_SLA'
                    then {{ elementary.edr_boolean_literal(false) }}
                    {# If deadline hasn't passed, don't fail yet #}
                    {% if not deadline_passed %}
                        when 1 = 1 then {{ elementary.edr_boolean_literal(false) }}
                    {% endif %}
                    else {{ elementary.edr_boolean_literal(true) }}
                end as is_failure,
                case
                    when sla_status = 'NOT_RUN'
                    then
                        'Model "{{ model_name }}" was not executed today. Expected before {{ formatted_sla_time }} {{ timezone }}.'
                    when sla_status = 'ALL_FAILED'
                    then
                        'Model "{{ model_name }}" ran '
                        || cast(total_runs_today as {{ elementary.edr_type_string() }})
                        || ' time(s) today but all executions failed.'
                    when sla_status = 'MISSED_SLA'
                    then
                        'Model "{{ model_name }}" first succeeded at ' || cast(
                            first_successful_run_utc
                            as {{ elementary.edr_type_string() }}
                        )
                        ||
                        ' UTC, which is after the SLA deadline of {{ formatted_sla_time }} {{ timezone }}.'
                    else
                        'Model "{{ model_name }}" met SLA - executed successfully before {{ formatted_sla_time }} {{ timezone }}.'
                end as result_description
            from sla_result
        )

    select
        model_name,
        model_unique_id,
        target_date,
        sla_time,
        timezone,
        sla_deadline_utc,
        sla_status,
        first_valid_run_utc,
        first_successful_run_utc,
        total_runs_today,
        successful_runs_today,
        result_description
    from final_result
    where is_failure = {{ elementary.edr_boolean_literal(true) }}

{% endmacro %}

macro.elementary.redshift__get_tables_fr.macro_sql:
{% macro redshift__get_tables_from_information_schema(schema_tuple) %}
    {%- set database_name, schema_name = schema_tuple %}

    with
        information_schema_tables as (

            select
                upper(table_catalog) as database_name,
                upper(table_schema) as schema_name,
                upper(table_name) as table_name
            from pg_catalog.svv_tables
            where
                upper(table_schema) = upper('{{ schema_name }}')
                and upper(table_catalog) = upper('{{ database_name }}')

        )

    select
        {{ elementary.full_table_name() }} as full_table_name,
        upper(database_name || '.' || schema_name) as full_schema_name,
        database_name,
        schema_name,
        table_name
    from information_schema_tables
{% endmacro %}

macro.elementary.get_columns_changes_que.name: get_columns_changes_query_generic
macro.elementary.get_columns_changes_que.macro_sql:
{% macro get_columns_changes_query_generic(
    full_table_name, cur, pre, include_added=True
) %}
    {%- set test_execution_id = elementary.get_test_execution_id() %}
    {%- set test_unique_id = elementary.get_test_unique_id() %}

    with
        cur as ({{ cur }}),

        pre as ({{ pre }}),

        type_changes as (

            {# Finding the columns that have changed type. #}
            select
                cur.full_table_name,
                'type_changed' as change,
                cur.column_name,
                cur.data_type as data_type,
                pre.data_type as pre_data_type,
                pre.detected_at
            from cur
            inner join
                pre
                on (
                    lower(cur.full_table_name) = lower(pre.full_table_name)
                    and lower(cur.column_name) = lower(pre.column_name)
                )
            where
                pre.data_type is not null
                and lower(cur.data_type) != lower(pre.data_type)

        ),

        {% if include_added %}
            columns_added as (

                {# This is the columns that have been added. #}
                select
                    full_table_name,
                    'column_added' as change,
                    column_name,
                    data_type,
                    {{ elementary.null_string() }} as pre_data_type,
                    detected_at as detected_at
                from cur
                where is_new = {{ elementary.edr_boolean_literal(true) }}

            ),
        {% endif %}

        columns_removed as (

            {# This is finding the columns that have been removed. #}
            select
                pre.full_table_name,
                'column_removed' as change,
                pre.column_name as column_name,
                {{ elementary.null_string() }} as data_type,
                pre.data_type as pre_data_type,
                pre.detected_at as detected_at
            from pre
            left join
                cur
                on (
                    lower(cur.full_table_name) = lower(pre.full_table_name)
                    and lower(cur.column_name) = lower(pre.column_name)
                )
            where cur.full_table_name is null and cur.column_name is null

        ),

        columns_removed_filter_deleted_tables as (

            {# This is filtering out the columns of tables that have been deleted. #}
            select
                removed.full_table_name,
                removed.change,
                removed.column_name,
                removed.data_type,
                removed.pre_data_type,
                removed.detected_at
            from columns_removed as removed
            join cur on (lower(removed.full_table_name) = lower(cur.full_table_name))

        ),

        all_column_changes as (

            {# Combining the results of the three queries into one table. #}
            select *
            from type_changes
            union all
            select *
            from columns_removed_filter_deleted_tables
            {% if include_added %}
                union all
                select *
                from columns_added
            {% endif %}
        ),

        column_changes_test_results as (

            {# This is the query that is creating the test results table, by formatting a description and adding id + detection time #}
            select
                {{
                    elementary.generate_surrogate_key(
                        [
                            "full_table_name",
                            "column_name",
                            "change",
                            "detected_at",
                        ]
                    )
                }} as data_issue_id,
                {{ elementary.datetime_now_utc_as_timestamp_column() }} as detected_at,
                {{ elementary.full_name_split("database_name") }},
                {{ elementary.full_name_split("schema_name") }},
                {{ elementary.full_name_split("table_name") }},
                column_name,
                'schema_change' as test_type,
                change as test_sub_type,
                {{ elementary.schema_change_description_column() }}
            from all_column_changes
            {% if elementary.is_tsql() %}
                {#- T-SQL does not support positional GROUP BY references.
                    Group by the 6 source columns from all_column_changes;
                    all 9 output columns are deterministic functions of these. -#}
                group by
                    full_table_name,
                    change,
                    column_name,
                    data_type,
                    pre_data_type,
                    detected_at
                {% else %} {{ dbt_utils.group_by(9) }}
                {% endif %}

        )

    {# Creating a unique id for each row in the table, and adding execution id #}
    select
        {{
            elementary.generate_surrogate_key(
                ["data_issue_id", elementary.const_as_string(test_execution_id)]
            )
        }} as id,
        {{ elementary.const_as_string(test_execution_id) }} as test_execution_id,
        {{ elementary.const_as_string(test_unique_id) }} as test_unique_id,
        *
    from column_changes_test_results

{%- endmacro %}

macro.elementary.default__freshness_metr.name: default__freshness_metric_query
macro.elementary.default__freshness_metr.macro_sql:
{% macro default__freshness_metric_query(metric, metric_properties) %}
    -- get ordered consecutive update timestamps in the source data
    with
        unique_timestamps as (
            select distinct monitored_table_timestamp_column as timestamp_val
            from partially_time_filtered_monitored_table
            order by 1
        ),

        -- compute freshness for every update as the time difference from the previous
        -- update
        consecutive_updates_freshness as (
            select
                timestamp_val as update_timestamp,
                {{ elementary._freshness_lag_expr() }} as freshness
            from unique_timestamps
        ),
        time_filtered_consecutive_updates_freshness as (
            select *
            from consecutive_updates_freshness
            where update_timestamp >= (select min(edr_bucket_start) from buckets)
        ),
        -- divide the freshness metrics above to buckets
        bucketed_consecutive_updates_freshness as (
            select edr_bucket_start, edr_bucket_end, update_timestamp, freshness
            from buckets
            cross join time_filtered_consecutive_updates_freshness
            where
                update_timestamp >= edr_bucket_start
                and update_timestamp < edr_bucket_end
        ),

        -- we also want to record the freshness at the end of each bucket as an
        -- additional point. By this we mean
        -- the time that passed since the last update in the bucket and the end of the
        -- bucket.
        bucket_end_freshness as (
            select
                edr_bucket_start,
                edr_bucket_end,
                max(timestamp_val) as update_timestamp,
                {{ elementary._bucket_end_freshness_expr() }} as freshness
            from buckets
            cross join unique_timestamps
            where timestamp_val < edr_bucket_end
            group by edr_bucket_start, edr_bucket_end
        ),

        -- create a single table with all the freshness values
        bucket_all_freshness_metrics as (
            select *
            from bucketed_consecutive_updates_freshness
            union all
            select *
            from bucket_end_freshness
        ),

        -- get all the freshness values, ranked by size (we use partition by and not
        -- group by, because we also want to have
        -- the associated timestamp as source value)
        bucket_freshness_ranked as (
            select
                *,
                row_number() over (
                    partition by edr_bucket_end
                    order by freshness is null, freshness desc
                ) as row_num
            from bucket_all_freshness_metrics
        )

    {{ elementary._freshness_final_select(metric) }}
    from bucket_freshness_ranked
    where row_num = 1
{% endmacro %}

        "0",

        "2",

        "6",

    ] %}
    {% set ns = namespace(

doc.dbt.__overview__.name: __overview__
doc.dbt.__overview__.block_contents:
### Welcome!

Welcome to the auto-generated documentation for your dbt project!

### Navigation

You can use the `Project` and `Database` navigation tabs on the left side of the window to explore the models
in your project.

#### Project Tab
The `Project` tab mirrors the directory structure of your dbt project. In this tab, you can see all of the
models defined in your dbt project, as well as models imported from dbt packages.

#### Database Tab
The `Database` tab also exposes your models, but in a format that looks more like a database explorer. This view
shows relations (tables and views) grouped into database schemas. Note that ephemeral models are _not_ shown
in this interface, as they do not exist in the database.

### Graph Exploration
You can click the blue icon on the bottom-right corner of the page to view the lineage graph of your models.

On model pages, you'll see the immediate parents and children of the model you're exploring. By clicking the `Expand`
button at the top-right of this lineage pane, you'll be able to see all of the models that are used to build,
or are built from, the model you're exploring.

Once expanded, you'll be able to use the `--select` and `--exclude` model selection syntax to filter the
models in the graph. For more information on model selection, check out the [dbt docs](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/model-selection-syntax).

Note that you can also right-click on models to interactively filter and explore the graph.

---

### More information

- [What is dbt](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/introduction)?
- Read the [dbt viewpoint](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/viewpoint)
- [Installation](https://docs.getdbt.com/docs/installation)
- Join the [dbt Community](https://www.getdbt.com/community/) for questions and discussion

exposure.mpi_analytics.ai_chatbot.name: ai_chatbot
exposure.mpi_analytics.ai_chatbot.description: AI-powered Q&A chatbot embedded in the legacy data review page. Lets users explore invoice data with natural language queries. Uses MartQueryExecutor to run validated SQL against mart tables. Backend: POST /qa/query.

exposure.mpi_analytics.analysis_page.name: analysis_page
exposure.mpi_analytics.analysis_page.description: Job-location cost analysis at /analysis. Shows cost breakdown by address and sheet (material type) with chart visualizations. Backend: POST /filter/aggregates-by-address-and-sheet, GET /filter/get-locations.

exposure.mpi_analytics.data_review_page.name: data_review_page
exposure.mpi_analytics.data_review_page.description: Main invoice browsing grid at /data-review. Supports filtering, sorting, pagination, PDF export, supplier reports, bulk edits, and void/restore. Backend: POST /filter, /filter/get_aggregates, /filter/by-column, /invoice-items/export, /filter/export-pdfs, /filter/supplier-report/export.

exposure.mpi_analytics.price_changes_pag.name: price_changes_page
exposure.mpi_analytics.price_changes_pag.description: Price change analysis at /price-changes and /price-changes/detail. Displays price increases and decreases over time per item-vendor pair, with drill-down into price history. Backend: POST /filter (price-change mode), /filter/price-history, /filter/download-price-history.

exposure.mpi_analytics.quickbooks_export.name: quickbooks_export_page
exposure.mpi_analytics.quickbooks_export.description: QuickBooks export workflow at /quickbooks-export. Previews invoice data, lets users edit before export, and pushes to QuickBooks. Backend: POST /quickbooks/preview-export, /quickbooks/export-from-preview, GET /quickbooks/unprocessed-date-range.

exposure.mpi_analytics.mappings_page.name: mappings_page
exposure.mpi_analytics.mappings_page.description: Unmapped items management at /mappings. Shows unmapped invoice items, mapping types, graph stats, mapping history timeline, and Google Sheet sync. Backend: /filter/unmapped-items, /mapping/mapping_types, /filter/unmapped-items/graph-stats, /mapping-history/item.

exposure.mpi_analytics.purchase_order_pa.name: purchase_order_page
exposure.mpi_analytics.purchase_order_pa.description: Purchase order price comparison at /purchase-order. Lets users upload or select PO items and compare against historical pricing. Backend: POST /purchase-orders/price-comparison.

exposure.mpi_analytics.supplier_comparis.name: supplier_comparison_page
exposure.mpi_analytics.supplier_comparis.description: Supplier comparison at /supplier-comparison. Compares item prices across suppliers with summary stats and exportable tables. Backend: POST /supplier-comparison/summary, /supplier-comparison/table, /supplier-comparison/export.
